terms.definition_short: A\*算法是一种启发式路径搜索算法，把从起点出发的实际代价和到目标的估计代价相加，在多条候选路径中高效找到最短路径。
terms.definition_short_en: The A\* algorithm is a heuristic path-search algorithm that efficiently finds the shortest route among multiple candidates by adding the actual cost from the starting point to the estimated cost to the target.

terms.definition_short: 消融实验通过删除或修改模型的某一部分，观察效果变化，用来确认每个组件到底贡献了多少。
terms.definition_short_en: An ablation study determines the exact contribution of each component by removing or modifying specific parts of a model and observing the resulting changes in performance.

terms.definition_short: 智能体是围绕大模型搭建的执行系统，核心是"观察→思考→行动"的循环，每一步决定是否继续、换工具或停止。
terms.definition_short_en: An AI agent is an execution system built around a foundation model. Its core is an 'observe-think-act' loop, deciding at each step whether to continue, switch tools, or stop.
terms.back_en: An intelligent system that autonomously perceives its environment, makes plans, uses tools, and executes tasks. It goes beyond single-turn Q&A by breaking down goals, calling tools, taking action, and self-correcting.
terms.definition_long_en:
The key difference between an AI agent and a standard chatbot is the ability to take action. When given a goal, an agent autonomously breaks down the necessary steps, selects the appropriate tools, evaluates the results of its actions, and determines what to do next.

Its core mechanism is an action loop: observe → think → act → observe. At every step, the system evaluates whether to proceed, switch tools, or stop and hand control back to a human user.

Typical examples include Claude Code, which can read code, write files, run commands, and fix bugs to complete an entire development workflow. Early attempts like AutoGPT also tried to autonomously break down and execute goals; although unstable at the time, they established a clear technical direction.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Agents transform large language models from mere chat interfaces into capable working partners. By calling tools, reading and writing files, browsing the web, and advancing multi-step tasks, they move AI beyond simple single-turn Q&A into autonomous execution.
terms.example_en:
· Claude Code autonomously reads code, writes files, runs commands, and fixes bugs.
· LangChain agents call various tools like search, calculators, and databases.
· AutoGPT automatically breaks down goals and executes multi-step tasks.
examples_en: Claude Code autonomously reads code, writes files, runs commands, and fixes bugs.
LangChain agents call various tools like search, calculators, and databases.
AutoGPT automatically breaks down goals and executes multi-step tasks.

terms.definition_short: AGI 是通用人工智能：一种仍在探索中的 AI 目标，指机器能跨领域理解任务、迁移经验、规划行动，并持续学习。
terms.definition_short_en: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is an AI goal still being explored. It refers to a machine's ability to understand tasks across domains, transfer experience, plan actions, and continuously learn.

terms.definition_short: AI 三要素指数据、算法和算力三件事同时成熟，AI 才更容易真正爆发。
terms.definition_short_en: The "AI Three Factors" refers to data, algorithms, and compute—the three core elements that must mature simultaneously for artificial intelligence to achieve true breakthroughs.

terms.definition_short: ALPAC 报告是 1966 年由美国自动语言处理咨询委员会提交的机器翻译评估报告，判定机器翻译性价比远不如人工。
terms.definition_short_en: The ALPAC Report was a 1966 evaluation submitted by the US Automatic Language Processing Advisory Committee, which concluded that machine translation was far less cost-effective than human translation.

terms.definition_short: AlphaEvolve 是用大模型提出候选方案、再用可验证的评估程序筛选并迭代的科研系统，适合结果可被测试或评分的问题。
terms.definition_short_en: AlphaEvolve is a scientific research system that uses large language models to propose candidate solutions, which are then screened and iterated by verifiable evaluation programs, making it suitable for problems where outcomes can be tested or scored.

terms.definition_short: AlphaFold：DeepMind 的蛋白质结构预测系统，从氨基酸序列直接算出三维形状。
terms.definition_short_en: An AI system developed by Google DeepMind that predicts the 3D structure of a protein directly from its amino acid sequence.
terms.back_en: Protein folding was an unsolved biological problem for 50 years. In 2020, AlphaFold used AI to solve it with near-perfect accuracy.
terms.definition_long_en:
AlphaFold represents a watershed moment for AI in biology.
In 2020, Google DeepMind introduced AlphaFold 2 at the CASP14 protein structure prediction competition. The results were groundbreaking: it achieved a median prediction accuracy of 0.96 angstroms, comparable to experimentally determined structures. In the eyes of the competition judges, this effectively solved the problem.
Why is predicting protein structure so difficult? The number of possible 3D shapes an amino acid sequence can fold into is staggering. According to Levinthal's paradox, a protein with 100 amino acids has more possible states than there are atoms in the universe. For the past 50 years, scientists relied on expensive and slow methods like X-ray crystallography and cryo-electron microscopy—determining a single structure could take a PhD student three years. AlphaFold reduced this process to mere minutes.
Under the hood, AlphaFold uses a Transformer variant combined with multiple sequence alignment and end-to-end training. However, its true significance lies beyond technical details: it proved that AI can replace decades of manual experimental labor in fundamental science.
terms.why_it_matters_en: AlphaFold marks a landmark achievement for AI in scientific discovery. It demonstrated to the broader scientific community that AI models can successfully decode and help us understand highly complex structures in the physical world.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as an AI microscope that helps scientists see the 3D shapes of proteins.
terms.example_en:
· In 2020, AlphaFold 2 achieved 0.96-angstrom accuracy at CASP14, which judges considered a solution to the problem.
· What used to take a PhD student three years to solve can now be done by AlphaFold in minutes.
· In 2024, AlphaFold 3 predicted protein interactions with DNA/RNA, pushing the technology further into drug discovery.
· Demis Hassabis and John Jumper won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this work.
· The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database freely released over 200 million protein structures for direct public access.
examples_en: In 2020, AlphaFold 2 achieved 0.96-angstrom accuracy at CASP14, which judges considered a solution to the problem.
What used to take a PhD student three years to solve can now be done by AlphaFold in minutes.
In 2024, AlphaFold 3 predicted protein interactions with DNA/RNA, pushing the technology further into drug discovery.
Demis Hassabis won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this work.
The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database freely released over 200 million protein structures for direct public access.

terms.definition_short: Artificial Intelligence，就是让机器学会看、听、读、写、判断和做事。
terms.definition_short_en: Artificial Intelligence is the capability that enables machines to see, hear, read, write, make decisions, and take action.

terms.definition_short: 注意力头是 Multi-Head Attention 的最小独立单元，每个头用自己的 Q/K/V 投影，专抓 token 间某一种关系。
terms.definition_short_en: An attention head is the smallest independent unit in multi-head attention, using its own Q/K/V (Query/Key/Value) projections to capture a specific type of relationship between tokens.

terms.definition_short: 注意力热力图把每一层、每个头的注意力权重可视化成颜色深浅，让模型内部"看哪里"这件事从数学变成图像。
terms.definition_short_en: An attention map visualizes the attention weights of each layer and head as color intensities, turning the mathematical process of where the model is "looking" into an intuitive image.

terms.definition_short: 注意力矩阵是注意力的数学本体：一个 N×N 的方阵，每行经 Softmax 后成为一个概率分布，加起来为 1。
terms.definition_short_en: The mathematical core of attention: an N×N square matrix where each row, after passing through a Softmax function, becomes a probability distribution that sums to 1.

terms.definition_short: 注意力变体指 Self-Attention、Cross-Attention、Causal-Attention 三种注意力模式，分别对应双向理解、跨序列对齐和自回归生成。
terms.definition_short_en: Attention mechanism variants refer to three primary modes—Self-Attention, Cross-Attention, and Causal-Attention—which correspond respectively to bidirectional understanding, cross-sequence alignment, and autoregressive generation.

terms.definition_short: 注意力汇指 LLM 在生成时把大量注意力权重压在开头几个 token 上，与这些 token 的语义重要性无关。
terms.definition_short_en: Attention sinks refer to the phenomenon where LLMs assign a massive amount of attention weight to the first few tokens during generation, regardless of their semantic importance.

terms.definition_short: 注意力可视化工具指 BertViz、exBERT 等，把 Transformer 的注意力权重画成热力图、连线图或神经元视图。
terms.definition_short_en: Attention visualization tools, such as BertViz and exBERT, map the attention weights of Transformer models into visual formats like heatmaps, connection graphs, or neuron views.

terms.definition_short: 注意力可视化把 Transformer 每一层的注意力权重画成图像，是调试和理解模型内部行为的主要手段。
terms.definition_short_en: Attention visualization plots the attention weights of each Transformer layer as an image, serving as a primary method for debugging and understanding the model's internal behavior.

terms.definition_short: Attention vs RNN 讲的是序列建模从串行到并行的转变——RNN 逐步传递、长序列易遗忘，Attention 全局并行、长距离依赖无衰减。
terms.definition_short_en: The shift from RNNs to Attention marks the transition from serial to parallel sequence modeling: RNNs process step-by-step and forget long sequences, while Attention computes globally in parallel without degrading long-range dependencies.

terms.definition_short: 自编码器由编码器和解码器组成，编码器把输入压成低维潜在表示，解码器再从潜在表示还原输出，靠"还原得越像越好"来学习。
terms.definition_short_en: An autoencoder consists of an encoder that compresses input into a low-dimensional latent representation, and a decoder that reconstructs the output, learning by making the reconstruction as accurate as possible.
terms.back_en: A model that compresses input into a smaller vector and then reconstructs it. By aiming to make the output match the original input as closely as possible, it learns to capture the essential features of the data during compression.
terms.definition_long_en:
Autoencoders solve the problem of representing large amounts of data in a very small space. Given a 28x28=784 pixel image of a handwritten digit, the encoder compresses it into 32 numbers (the latent representation), and the decoder uses these 32 numbers to reconstruct the 784-pixel image. The training objective is to make the reconstructed image as identical to the original as possible.

This compression is not random. The encoder must learn to capture highly discriminative information (such as which pixels determine it is a 7 rather than a 1) and discard irrelevant information (like background noise). The resulting 32 numbers represent the "essential features" of the data.

It has three main applications: dimensionality reduction, compressing high-dimensional data to 2-3 dimensions for visualization and clustering; denoising, where noise is added to training data so the autoencoder learns to reconstruct a clean version; and anomaly detection, where models trained on normal data will show high reconstruction errors for anomalies. Autoencoders later evolved into Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), which allow sampling, and eventually diffusion models, serving as the starting point for this entire lineage of generative models.
terms.why_it_matters_en: The autoencoder is a classic paradigm of representation learning. It enables models to automatically learn which features are worth paying attention to, and serves as the foundation for modern generative models like VAEs and diffusion models.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as compressing then decompressing—where the model learns what features matter most during the compression phase.
terms.example_en:
· Compressing 784 pixels into 32 numbers and reconstructing them: the encoder captures the essence, and the decoder restores it.
· Dimensionality reduction: compressing high-dimensional data to 2-3D for clustering; Denoising: training to restore clean versions; Anomaly detection: high reconstruction error indicates an anomaly.
· Autoencoder → VAE (sampleable) → Diffusion models: the entire lineage of generative models stems from here.
examples_en: Compressing 28x28=784 pixels into 32 numbers and reconstructing them: the encoder captures the essence, and the decoder restores it.
Dimensionality reduction: compressing high-dimensional data to 2-3D for clustering. Denoising: training to restore clean versions. Anomaly detection: high reconstruction error = anomaly.
Autoencoder → VAE (sampleable) → Diffusion models: the entire family of generative models follows this lineage.
Using an autoencoder instead of PCA for dimensionality reduction: non-linear dimensionality reduction yields much better results.
Using a denoising autoencoder for anomaly detection: trained on normal data, a sudden spike in reconstruction error indicates an anomaly.

terms.definition_short: 自动化的就业悖论指：机器替代了重复性任务，但相关岗位的数量未必下降，因为自动化同时重塑了就业结构。
terms.definition_short_en: The Paradox of Automation refers to the phenomenon where machines replace repetitive tasks, yet the number of related jobs does not necessarily decline because automation simultaneously reshapes the employment structure.

terms.definition_short: 贝叶斯定理：P(A|B) = P(B|A)×P(A)/P(B)，从结果反推原因的概率公式，朴素贝叶斯、贝叶斯优化、变分推断都建立在它之上。
terms.definition_short_en: Bayes' Theorem, expressed as P(A|B) = P(B|A)×P(A)/P(B), is a probability formula for inferring causes from observed outcomes. It forms the foundation for Naive Bayes, Bayesian optimization, and variational inference.

terms.definition_short: CNN 池化指每次把特征图的空间尺寸减半、通道数翻倍的操作，把空间信息转化到通道维度。
terms.definition_short_en: CNN pooling is an operation that halves the spatial dimensions of a feature map while doubling its channel count, effectively converting spatial information into the channel dimension.

terms.definition_short: CNN vs Transformer 是计算机视觉的两代架构之争——CNN 靠局部性，Transformer 靠全局注意力。
terms.definition_short_en: The CNN vs Transformer debate represents a shift between two generations of computer vision architectures: CNNs rely on locality, while Transformers leverage global attention.
terms.front_en: How do CNNs and Transformers differ in computer vision?
terms.back_en: CNNs use convolutional sliding windows and local inductive biases, excelling on smaller datasets. Transformers use self-attention for global modeling, outperforming CNNs when trained on massive amounts of data.
terms.definition_long_en:
A CNN's inductive bias is locality; each convolutional kernel only looks at a small region, learning edges, textures, and local shapes. When data is scarce, this bias is an advantage because the model doesn't need to learn from scratch that "nearby pixels are more closely related."

Transformers lack this spatial inductive bias. They process all pixels simultaneously and require massive amounts of data to learn the locality that comes built-in with CNNs. In 2020, ViT proved that Transformers could surpass CNNs after being trained on 14 million images, sparking a migration toward Transformers in the vision field.

By 2024, the landscape became scenario-dependent: CNNs remain strong for small datasets, while Transformers dominate large ones. The two are also blending—ConvNeXt modernizes CNNs to resemble Transformers, while Swin Transformer introduces local windows into Transformers. For model selection, the ResNet family is used for small data, the ViT family for large data, and ConvNeXt for a hybrid approach.
terms.why_it_matters_en: The CNN vs Transformer evolution marks the shift in computer vision from local processing to global modeling, dictating how practitioners select models based on the scale of their available data.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as two types of architects: CNNs look at the bricks first, while Transformers look at the entire blueprint.
terms.example_en:
· CNN's local convolutions have an advantage on small datasets, while Transformer's global attention is stronger on large datasets.
· In 2020, ViT surpassed CNNs using 14 million images; by 2024, the ResNet family is chosen for small data, the ViT family for large data, and ConvNeXt for hybrid architectures.
examples_en: CNNs excel on small datasets via local convolutions, while Transformers dominate large datasets using global attention.
In 2020, ViT surpassed CNNs using 14 million images. By 2024, CNNs remain strong for small data, Transformers for large data, with hybrid architectures offering a middle ground.
For model selection: use the ResNet family for small datasets, the ViT family for large datasets, and ConvNeXt for hybrid approaches.

terms.definition_short: AI 共同科学家指用 AI 帮研究者生成假设、设计实验、检查证据链的一类系统。
terms.definition_short_en: An AI Co-Scientist is a type of system designed to assist researchers by generating hypotheses, designing experiments, and verifying evidence chains.

terms.definition_short: 混淆矩阵是分类模型的底表，TP、TN、FP、FN 四个数字一目了然，所有分类评估指标都从它衍生。
terms.definition_short_en: A confusion matrix is the foundational table for evaluating classification models. It clearly displays TP, TN, FP, and FN, serving as the basis from which all other classification metrics are derived.

terms.definition_short: 交叉注意力是解码器与编码器之间的信息桥，解码器的 Query 去查编码器的 Key 和 Value，实现跨序列对齐。
terms.definition_short_en: Cross-Attention acts as an information bridge between the encoder and decoder, where the decoder's Query interacts with the encoder's Keys and Values to achieve cross-sequence alignment.
terms.back_en: As the decoder generates each output word, it looks back at the encoder's representation of the input to determine which parts are most relevant to the current word. This is cross-attention.
terms.definition_long_en:
Cross-Attention applies the attention mechanism across different modules. As the decoder generates each output token, it uses its current Query to compute against the Keys and Values from the encoder's output, essentially asking: which parts of the input sentence are important for this specific token?

This is most intuitive in machine translation. After the encoder processes an English sentence, it generates an understanding of each word. When the decoder starts writing in French, Cross-Attention checks which word in the input aligns with the current French word being generated, locating the relevant input segment.

Cross-Attention only appears in Encoder-Decoder architectures, such as T5, BART, and the original Transformer. GPT models do not use it because they are Decoder-Only and lack an encoder to cross-reference. However, Cross-Attention has seen a revival in multimodal models: during image generation, the decoder uses the text prompt as the input source for Cross-Attention, aligning text and image representations.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Cross-Attention is the information bridge between the encoder and decoder. It determines how the model extracts information from the input during generation tasks, making it a critical component for translation, summarization, and multimodal generation.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the decoder looking back at the encoder—glancing at the input for every word it writes.
terms.example_en:
· In translation, as the decoder writes each French word, Cross-Attention helps it find the corresponding word in the English input.
· GPT lacks Cross-Attention (as a Decoder-Only model without an encoder), whereas T5 and BART have it.
· Cross-Attention is revived in multimodal models, using text as the input source during image generation.
examples_en: Self-Attention computes within itself, while Cross-Attention computes across modules—the decoder's Query checks the encoder's Keys and Values.
During translation, the decoder can glance at the English input for every French word it writes—finding the input segment that corresponds to the current output.
GPT does not have Cross-Attention (Decoder-Only models lack encoders), but T5 and BART do.
Cross-Attention is revived in multimodal models—during image generation, the decoder uses text as the Cross-Attention input source.

terms.definition_short: 维度诅咒指数据维度越高、数据越稀疏，距离度量逐渐失效，机器学习里特征太多反而越糟。
terms.definition_short_en: The curse of dimensionality refers to the phenomenon where increasing data dimensions causes sparsity and renders distance metrics ineffective, meaning that adding too many features can actually degrade machine learning performance.

terms.definition_short: 控制论是维纳提出的关于控制与通信的工程科学，为 AI 提供了反馈和学习的基础框架。
terms.definition_short_en: Cybernetics is an engineering science proposed by Norbert Wiener focused on control and communication, providing the foundational framework for feedback and learning in AI.

terms.definition_short: 深度学习是机器学习的一个子领域，用多层神经网络加大量数据加反向传播训练，让模型自己从数据里学特征。
terms.definition_short_en: Deep learning is a subfield of machine learning that combines multi-layer neural networks, massive datasets, and backpropagation training to enable models to automatically learn features from data.

terms.definition_short: DistilBERT 是 BERT 的轻量蒸馏版，参数少、速度快、性能几乎不降，适合部署到移动端和边缘设备。
terms.definition_short_en: DistilBERT is a lightweight, distilled version of BERT that features fewer parameters and faster speeds with minimal performance loss, making it ideal for deployment on mobile and edge devices.

terms.definition_short: Encoder-Decoder 完整架构指同时使用编码器和解码器的 Transformer 变体，适合输入到输出的转换任务。
terms.definition_short_en: The Encoder-Decoder architecture is a Transformer variant that utilizes both an encoder and a decoder, making it highly suitable for input-to-output conversion tasks.

terms.definition_short: Extrapolation 是用小规模实验里的规律，预测更大规模模型、数据或算力下会发生什么。
terms.definition_short_en: Extrapolation is the process of using patterns observed in small-scale experiments to predict outcomes when scaling up models, data, or compute.

terms.definition_short: 特征工程是从原始数据到模型可理解输入之间的桥梁，手工设计或自动学习，深度学习让这个过程自动化。
terms.definition_short_en: Feature engineering acts as a bridge between raw data and model-understandable inputs, transitioning from manual design in traditional machine learning to automated extraction in deep learning.

terms.definition_short: 框架问题指符号 AI 时代的一个根本困境：系统必须显式处理每一条背景知识，却无法判断哪些该忽略。
terms.definition_short_en: The Frame Problem refers to a fundamental dilemma from the symbolic AI era: a system must explicitly process all background knowledge but cannot determine which facts to ignore.

terms.definition_short: GPT 系列论文解读梳理从 GPT-1 预训练加微调到 GPT-4 多模态的技术路线，每篇论文解决一个根本问题。
terms.definition_short_en: An overview of the GPT series papers traces the technical roadmap from GPT-1's pre-training and fine-tuning to GPT-4's multimodality, with each paper addressing a fundamental problem.

terms.definition_short: 乔治·布林（1815-1864）是英国数学家和逻辑学家。他创立的布尔代数是一切数字电路、计算机和人工智能的数学地基。
terms.definition_short_en: George Boole (1815–1864) was an English mathematician and logician. His creation, Boolean algebra, serves as the mathematical foundation for all digital circuits, computers, and artificial intelligence.

terms.definition_short: 戈登 vs 奇点论是一场关于技术进步是否已触顶的辩论——戈登认为第三次工业革命的红利已耗尽，奇点论者认为指数增长只是被推迟。
terms.definition_short_en: The Gordon vs Singularity debate centers on whether technological progress has peaked: Gordon argues the Third Industrial Revolution's dividends are exhausted, while Singularity proponents believe exponential growth is merely delayed.

terms.definition_short: GPT-4V 是 GPT-4 的视觉版本，把图片切成 patches 变成视觉 token 与文字 token 一起喂给模型，让 LLM 长出眼睛。
terms.definition_short_en: GPT-4V is the vision-enabled version of GPT-4. It divides images into patches, converts them into visual tokens, and feeds them into the model alongside text tokens, effectively giving the LLM 'eyes'.
terms.back_en: The vision version of GPT-4. By attaching a vision encoder to the text-only model, it can process images, charts, screenshots, and PDFs, making it the first mainstream multimodal LLM product.
terms.definition_long_en:
OpenAI released GPT-4V (Vision) in 2023. It works by attaching a vision encoder to the text-only GPT-4 model. It slices images into patches, converts them into visual tokens, and feeds them into the model alongside text tokens.

It can perform image comprehension, chart analysis, UI-to-code conversion, OCR, and handwriting recognition. It retains the same reasoning capabilities as GPT-4, just with added visual input. In the API, the vision mode bills based on image tokens, meaning larger images cost more to process.

The significance of GPT-4V lies in proving that visual understanding can be bolted onto an LLM without needing to train a standalone vision model from scratch, marking the first step toward mainstream multimodal LLMs. Later, GPT-4o further unified vision, audio, and text into a native multimodal architecture.
terms.why_it_matters_en: As the first mainstream multimodal LLM product, GPT-4V proved that visual understanding capabilities could be successfully bolted onto an existing language model without the need to train a standalone vision model from scratch.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as GPT-4 putting on glasses—it can now see images, charts, and screenshots.
terms.example_en:
· 2023: GPT-4V attaches a vision encoder to the text-only GPT-4, mixing image patches converted into visual tokens with text.
· Features include image comprehension, chart analysis, UI-to-code, OCR, and handwriting recognition; the API bills by image tokens.
examples_en: 2023: GPT-4V attaches a vision encoder to the text-only GPT-4, converting images into visual tokens to mix with text.
Capabilities include image comprehension, chart analysis, UI-to-code, OCR, and handwriting recognition. The API bills by image tokens, with larger images costing more.

terms.definition_short: 图数据库以节点和边存储数据，节点是实体、边是关系，是知识图谱、社交网络、推荐系统的原生存储。
terms.definition_short_en: A graph database stores data using nodes for entities and edges for relationships, serving as the native storage architecture for knowledge graphs, social networks, and recommendation systems.

terms.definition_short: GNN 是图神经网络，在社交网络、分子结构、知识图谱这种非网格数据上做深度学习。
terms.definition_short_en: A Graph Neural Network (GNN) applies deep learning to non-grid data structures, such as social networks, molecular structures, and knowledge graphs.

terms.definition_short: 图神经网络是处理图结构数据的神经网络，应用于分子、社交网络、推荐系统、知识图谱等非网格非序列数据。
terms.definition_short_en: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are neural networks designed to process graph-structured data, applied to non-grid and non-sequential data such as molecules, social networks, recommendation systems, and knowledge graphs.

terms.definition_short: 启发式搜索是用启发式函数引导搜索方向的方法，避免穷举，是"有效的老式人工智能"（GOFAI）的核心技术。
terms.definition_short_en: Heuristic search is a method that uses heuristic functions to guide the search direction and avoid exhaustive enumeration, serving as a core technology of Good Old-Fashioned AI (GOFAI).
terms.back_en: A method that uses rules of thumb to prune impossible branches in a vast possibility space to quickly find answers. It serves as the problem-solving cornerstone of Good Old-Fashioned AI (GOFAI).
terms.definition_long_en:
Heuristic search was the fundamental methodology of early AI. In 1976, Allen Newell and Herbert A. Simon proposed the physical symbol system hypothesis, laying its philosophical foundation: intelligence operates on symbols, and a physical symbol system has the necessary and sufficient means for general intelligent action. The most typical implementation of "operating on symbols" is search.

By studying human behavior, they proposed the symbolic search method: human problem-solving is essentially a search through a "space of possibilities." A good search strategy requires rules of thumb (heuristics) to prune impossible branches; otherwise, the search space would explode exponentially. Newell and Simon were awarded the 1975 Turing Award for these contributions.

One of the most famous achievements of heuristic search is the Shakey the robot project. Developed at the Stanford Research Institute, Shakey was the world's first autonomous mobile robot. It utilized the A* algorithm—currently known as the optimal method for finding the shortest path between two points. Shakey could discover and push target objects within its highly structured world and move around according to pre-planned routes.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Heuristic search is the foundational technology of GOFAI and serves as the basis for understanding classic AI methods such as the A* algorithm, search trees, and game tree pruning.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as a maze compass—a search technique that uses rules of thumb to avoid dead ends.
terms.example_en:
· Newell and Simon proposed the physical symbol system hypothesis, arguing that the essence of intelligence is symbolic search, with heuristic functions helping to prune the search space.
· The Shakey robot used the A* algorithm for heuristic search, serving as a classic implementation of shortest-path search.
examples_en:
The core methodology of early AI that uses "rules of thumb" to quickly find answers in a vast possibility space, serving as the problem-solving cornerstone of GOFAI.

Heuristic search is a core technology of Good Old-Fashioned AI (GOFAI).

terms.definition_short: KAN 基于 Kolmogorov-Arnold 表示定理，把传统 MLP 里"节点上的固定激活函数"换成"边上的可学激活函数"，让网络结构更透明、更省参数，适合小数据回归和符号回归。
terms.definition_short_en: Based on the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, KAN replaces the fixed activation functions on nodes found in traditional MLPs with learnable activation functions on edges. This creates a more transparent and parameter-efficient network, particularly suited for small-data and symbolic regression.

terms.definition_short: 标签编码是给类别变量分配整数的简单编码方法，适用于树模型，但在线性模型和神经网络上要用 One-Hot 替代。
terms.definition_short_en: Label encoding is a simple method that assigns integers to categorical variables. It works well for tree-based models but should be replaced by one-hot encoding when using linear models or neural networks.

terms.definition_short: 熄灯工厂指完全自动化的生产线，是制造业自动化的理想形态，但现实与愿景之间存在巨大落差。
terms.definition_short_en: A lights-out factory is a fully automated production line representing the ideal state of manufacturing automation, though a significant gap remains between this vision and reality.

terms.definition_short: 线性注意力通过重写 softmax 公式、用核函数近似，把注意力的内存和时间从 n² 降到 n，是处理长序列的折中方案。
terms.definition_short_en: Linear Attention reduces the time and memory complexity of attention from O(n²) to O(n) by rewriting the softmax formula with kernel function approximations, offering a trade-off solution for processing long sequences.

terms.definition_short: 液态神经网络用微分方程动态控制权重，让网络在推理时也能自适应新环境，是 AI 从固态到流态的演进尝试。
terms.definition_short_en: Liquid Neural Networks use differential equations to dynamically adjust their weights, allowing them to adapt to new environments during inference. This represents an evolutionary shift from static to fluid AI models.

terms.definition_short: LLM-as-Judge 是用大模型评估大模型输出质量的方法，包括成对比较、单回答评分和按标准评价三种方式。
terms.definition_short_en: LLM-as-Judge is a method of using a large language model to evaluate the output quality of other models through pairwise comparisons, single-answer scoring, or criteria-based evaluation.
terms.front_en: What does the term LLM-as-Judge mean?
terms.back_en: Using a large language model to score the outputs of another model, replacing human annotation for automated quality assessment. GPT-4's judgments have shown a correlation coefficient of over 0.9 with human consensus.
terms.definition_long_en:
The most accurate way to evaluate a foundation model is human scoring, but manual annotation is slow and expensive. LLM-as-Judge addresses this by using a strong model (typically GPT-4) to evaluate outputs, either by choosing the better of two responses or scoring a single answer.

A landmark validation of this method was the 2023 Chatbot Arena by LMSYS. When GPT-4 judged responses from two anonymous models, its preferences achieved a >0.9 correlation with human consensus, transforming LLM-as-Judge into an engineering standard.

The approach uses three formats: pairwise comparison (selecting the better of two answers, which is highly stable), single-answer scoring (rating one response, though prone to biases like favoring longer answers), and criteria-based evaluation (scoring against specific rubrics like accuracy or safety for higher precision).

Practitioners must mitigate three main biases: position bias (favoring the first answer presented), verbosity bias (preferring longer responses), and self-enhancement bias (where a model favors its own outputs). These are typically addressed through position randomization and length control.
terms.why_it_matters_en: LLM-as-Judge makes large-scale, automated evaluation possible by dramatically reducing the time and cost associated with human annotation. It serves as a critical piece of AI evaluation infrastructure alongside RLHF, enabling developers to rapidly iterate and benchmark foundation models with high consistency.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as AI grading AI: fast and cheap, but beware of the judge favoring its own outputs.
terms.example_en:
· The 2023 Chatbot Arena demonstrated that GPT-4's judgments have a >0.9 correlation with human consensus.
· Three formats: pairwise comparison is the most stable, single-answer scoring has biases, and criteria-based evaluation is more precise.
· Three biases: position, verbosity, and self-enhancement, which are mitigated using position randomization and length control.
examples_en: The 2023 Chatbot Arena proved the viability of LLM-as-Judge, with GPT-4 achieving a >0.9 correlation with human consensus.
Three evaluation formats: pairwise comparison, single-answer scoring (prone to bias), and criteria-based evaluation (more precise).
Limitations include position bias, verbosity bias, and self-enhancement bias, as the judge is often also a competitor.
Large-scale evaluation often uses LLMs for initial screening and humans for final review, employing position randomization and length control to reduce bias.

terms.definition_short: LLM 即工具指 LLM 作为基础设施被编排进更大的软件系统里，通过 Function Calling 和 Agent 架构被产品调用，而非作为聊天窗口存在。
terms.definition_short_en: LLM-as-Tool refers to orchestrating LLMs as infrastructure within larger software systems. Instead of acting as standalone chat windows, they are called by products via function calling and agent architectures.

terms.definition_short: LLM 压缩通过量化、剪枝、蒸馏三重手段把大模型压到能在消费级设备和边缘端运行，是本地部署的工程基础。
terms.definition_short_en: LLM compression shrinks large models using quantization, pruning, and distillation so they can run on consumer devices and edge hardware, serving as the engineering foundation for local deployment.

terms.definition_short: LLM 评测用标准化的基准和多维评分体系衡量大模型能力，从单基准分数演进到能力画像。
terms.definition_short_en: LLM evaluation measures foundation model capabilities using standardized benchmarks and multidimensional scoring systems, evolving from single-benchmark scores to comprehensive capability profiles.

terms.definition_short: LLM 多语言指大模型同时处理多种语言的能力，依赖训练数据的多语言配比和 Tokenizer 优化，分为英文为主、中文优先、多语言均衡三类。
terms.definition_short_en: LLM multilingual capability refers to a foundation model's ability to process multiple languages simultaneously. It relies on training data ratios and tokenizer optimization, and is generally categorized into English-dominant, Chinese-first, and balanced multilingual models.

terms.definition_short: LLM 安全通过输入过滤、对齐训练、护栏系统、人工反馈四层纵深防御，保护模型不被恶意利用。
terms.definition_short_en: LLM security protects models from malicious exploitation through a four-layer defense-in-depth strategy: input filtering, alignment training, guardrail systems, and human feedback.

terms.definition_short: MLP-Mixer 用纯全连接层替代 CNN 的卷积和 ViT 的注意力，靠 Channel-Mixing 和 Token-Mixing 两个 MLP 交替处理，是极简架构的代表性尝试。
terms.definition_short_en: MLP-Mixer is a representative attempt at a minimalist architecture that replaces the convolutions of CNNs and the attention mechanisms of ViTs with pure fully connected layers, relying entirely on alternating Channel-Mixing and Token-Mixing MLPs.

terms.definition_short: MLP vs Transformer 是架构选择的两个极端——MLP 固定全连接无归纳偏置，Transformer 动态注意力有全局视野，各自适合不同数据规模和任务。
terms.definition_short_en: MLP and Transformer represent two extremes in architectural design: MLP relies on fixed, fully connected layers with no inductive bias, while Transformer uses dynamic attention for a global receptive field. Each suits different data scales and tasks.

terms.definition_short: 模型堆叠是集成学习的金字塔尖，不同类型基模型并联预测、再串一个元模型学最佳加权方式，比 Bagging 和 Boosting 更进一步。
terms.definition_short_en: Model stacking is the pinnacle of ensemble learning, going a step beyond bagging and boosting by using diverse base models to generate parallel predictions, which are then fed into a meta-model that learns the optimal weighting strategy.

terms.definition_short: 摩尔定律指集成电路晶体管数量每两年翻一倍的规律，是行业自我实现的预言，2015 年后开始放缓，2024 年黄仁勋公开宣称"已死"。
terms.definition_short_en: Moore's Law states that the number of transistors on an integrated circuit doubles every two years. This industry self-fulfilling prophecy began slowing down after 2015, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly declared it "dead" in 2024.

terms.definition_short: MQA 让所有 Query 头共用同一组 K/V，KV 头数等于 1，显存省 H 倍，但精度有损。
terms.definition_short_en: MQA forces all query heads to share a single set of Keys and Values (KV heads = 1), reducing memory usage by a factor of H, though at the cost of some accuracy.

terms.definition_short: 多模态 AI 同时处理多种信息形式，把文本、图像、音频、视频送到一个模型内融合理解，是 AI 从单一感官走向多感官融合的演进。
terms.definition_short_en: Multimodal AI processes multiple forms of information simultaneously, fusing text, images, audio, and video within a single model for integrated understanding. It represents AI's evolution from single-sensory processing to multi-sensory fusion.

terms.definition_short: 多模态大模型接收图声视作为输入、输出文字或语音，分拼接派（后挂编码器）和原生派（预训练就混多模态）两条技术路线。
terms.definition_short_en: Multimodal LLMs accept images, audio, and video as inputs to output text or speech. They follow two main technical routes: a stitched approach using add-on encoders, or a native approach that mixes modalities during pre-training.
terms.back_en: An LLM that simultaneously understands text, images, audio, and video. GPT-4o and Gemini are prime examples: you can turn on your camera and speak directly while the AI sees your actions, listens to your voice, and responds.
terms.definition_long_en:
Traditional LLMs are text-only: you type questions, and they type answers. Multimodal LLMs effectively give AI eyes and ears.

GPT-4o exemplifies this: you can turn on your camera and ask, 'What is this in my hand?' The AI observes your video feed in real time, listens, and replies with speech. Gemini can simultaneously analyze a video's visuals, voiceover, and subtitles, while Claude 3.5 Sonnet can process images and PDFs.

Technically, there are two main approaches. The 'stitched' method trains a text-only LLM first, then attaches visual and audio encoders to tokenize media before feeding it into the prompt. GPT-4V took this path, which is easier to implement. The 'native' approach mixes text, image, and audio tokens right from the pre-training phase. Gemini follows this route, integrating visual information more deeply into the model's language capabilities.

The 2024-2025 period marks a boom for multimodal LLMs. GPT-4o achieved real-time multimodal dialogue, Gemini 2.0 integrated multimodal capabilities into agent architectures, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet excels at analyzing documents. Model selection depends on the use case: native multimodal models like Gemini are often preferred for heavy video analysis, while GPT-4o is highly effective for text-heavy tasks with occasional visual inputs.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Multimodal LLMs transition AI from text-only processing to simultaneously seeing, hearing, and speaking. This is a crucial step toward creating universal AI assistants, as humans naturally communicate using multiple senses.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as AI using eyes and ears simultaneously—seeing, hearing, and speaking just like a real person.
terms.example_en:
· GPT-4o observes video, listens, and responds with speech in real time; Gemini analyzes video visuals, voiceovers, and subtitles; Claude 3.5 processes PDFs.
· The stitched approach trains text first and adds encoders later (GPT-4V), while the native approach mixes text, images, and audio during training (Gemini).
· The 2024-2025 boom: GPT-4o for real-time dialogue, Gemini 2.0 for agents, and Claude 3.5 for PDF analysis.
examples_en: Traditional LLMs only process text. Multimodal LLMs accept images, audio, and video to output text and speech, effectively giving AI eyes and ears.
The stitched approach trains text first and adds encoders later (GPT-4V), while the native approach mixes text, images, and audio during training (Gemini).
The 2024-2025 boom: GPT-4o for real-time dialogue, Gemini 2.0 for agents, and Claude 3.5 for PDF analysis.
Use Gemini's native multimodality for heavy image and video analysis, and GPT-4o for primarily text-based tasks with occasional visual inputs.

terms.definition_short: NER 从文字中识别人名、地名、组织名、日期、金额等具体实体，是信息提取的基础任务。
terms.definition_short_en: Named Entity Recognition (NER) identifies and classifies specific entities in text—such as people, locations, organizations, dates, and monetary values—serving as the foundational task for information extraction.

terms.definition_short: NLP 用统计、表示学习和上下文建模让机器在语言任务上表现得越来越像理解，是 ChatGPT 之前 AI 处理人类语言的总称。
terms.definition_short_en: NLP uses statistics, representation learning, and context modeling to make machines perform as if they understand language. It is the umbrella term for how AI processed human language long before ChatGPT.

terms.definition_short: NLU 是 NLP 的一个子方向，关注机器怎样理解词语、句子、上下文、意图和实体关系，是搜索、问答、客服、翻译的基础能力。
terms.definition_short_en: A subfield of NLP, NLU focuses on how machines comprehend words, sentences, context, intent, and entity relationships, serving as the foundational capability for search, Q&A, customer service, and translation.

terms.definition_short: 神经缩放定律指神经网络能力随参数、数据、计算量的幂律增长，从 NLP 扩展到视觉、强化学习、多模态等领域。
terms.definition_short_en: The Neural Scaling Law states that a neural network's performance improves as a power-law function of its parameters, data, and compute, a principle extending from NLP to vision, reinforcement learning, and multimodal domains.

terms.definition_short: NLP 简史记录自然语言处理从规则时代到统计时代到深度学习时代到 LLM 时代的四段演进。
terms.definition_short_en: The brief history of NLP chronicles the four-stage evolution of natural language processing: from the rule-based era to statistical methods, deep learning, and finally the LLM era.
terms.front_en: What is the brief history of NLP?
terms.back_en: A 70-year evolution across four stages: relying on rules for Russian translation in the 1950s, statistical methods in the 1990s, deep learning in the 2010s, and large language models in the 2020s.
terms.definition_long_en:
The 70-year history of NLP is a journey from hand-crafted rules to autonomous model learning.

The 1950s to 1980s marked the rule-based era. A milestone was the 1954 Georgetown-IBM experiment, which used six grammar rules and 250 words to translate Russian into English, prompting media claims that machine translation would be solved within five years. However, rules could not capture the complexity of real language, leading to a dead end.

The 1990s to 2010s ushered in the statistical era. The paradigm shifted to calculating probabilities from parallel corpora. Early systems like IBM Models 1-5 and Google Translate relied on these methods. While they processed new sentences without new rules, translations were often unnatural because the models lacked semantic understanding.

The 2010s introduced the deep learning era. RNNs and LSTMs processed sequences, and in 2014, Seq2Seq with attention mechanisms dramatically improved translation. In 2018, BERT achieved bidirectional understanding to set new SOTA records, while GPT-1 introduced autoregressive pre-training.

The 2020s is the era of large language models (LLMs). GPT-3 served as a watershed moment, making "one model for all tasks" a reality. Instead of training separate models for specific tasks, a single LLM can now handle diverse NLP workloads via prompts.
terms.why_it_matters_en: The brief history of NLP is key to understanding AI's evolution. From rules to statistics, deep learning, and LLMs, every leap forward represents a victory for the paradigm of letting models learn autonomously.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as four stages over 70 years: rules, statistics, deep learning, and LLMs—each letting models learn more autonomously.
terms.example_en:
· 1954 Georgetown-IBM experiment: Translated Russian using 6 rules and 250 words, leading the media to claim translation would be solved in 3-5 years.
· 1990s: Statistical methods learned probabilities from data; 2010s: Deep learning with BERT/GPT; 2020s: Zero-shot generalization with LLMs.
· GPT-3 as a watershed: NLP shifted from "one model per task" to "one model for all tasks."
examples_en: 1950s: Rule-based translation using 6 grammar rules for Russian; 1990s: Statistical methods learning probabilities from data; 2010s: Deep learning with BERT/GPT; 2020s: Zero-shot generalization with LLMs.
1954 Georgetown-IBM experiment: Translated Russian using 6 rules and 250 words—leading the media to claim translation would be solved in three to five years.
NLP shifted from "one model per task" to "one model for all tasks"—GPT-3 was the watershed moment.
Use BERT for simple classification, GPT for generation, and T5 for translation and summarization—do not use LLM APIs for small tasks.

terms.definition_short: 开源 LLM 指开放权重的大语言模型，零 API 成本、零数据泄漏、可 fine-tune，2024 年在多数基准上追近闭源模型。
terms.definition_short_en: Open-source LLMs are open-weight large language models that offer zero API costs, no data leakage, and fine-tuning capabilities, having closely trailed closed-source models across most benchmarks in 2024.
terms.back_en: From Llama to Mistral and DeepSeek, open-source large language models have caught up to closed-source counterparts as direct competitors. In 2024, Llama 3 70B trailed GPT-4 by less than 10% on most benchmarks.
terms.definition_long_en:
Open-source LLMs are the primary vehicle for AI democratization. In 2023, Meta released Llama 2—the first major model weights with a commercial license—allowing everyday users to run a highly capable foundation model locally.

The ecosystem surged over the following year. In late 2023, Mistral's MoE-based Mixtral 8x7B outperformed Llama 70B using only 13B active parameters during inference. By 2024, Llama 3 70B trailed GPT-4 by less than 10% on most benchmarks. The gap between open and closed models has narrowed drastically, transforming open-source LLMs from cheap alternatives into direct competitors.

These models offer three core advantages: zero API costs for unlimited high-frequency usage, zero data leakage risks via local deployment for sensitive industries, and the ability to fine-tune models for specific business tasks like coding or customer service.

However, challenges remain. They require dedicated GPUs for VRAM, demand complex operational overhead compared to simple API calls, and face rapid obsolescence due to fast-paced updates. When selecting an open-source LLM, evaluate benchmark scores, hardware requirements, and Chinese language capabilities, where models like DeepSeek and Qwen excel.
terms.why_it_matters_en: The open-source release of Llama 2 in 2023 was a watershed moment. As the first major model weights with a commercial license, it turned AI democratization from a slogan into reality, drastically narrowing the gap between open-source and closed-source models ever since.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the vehicle for AI democratization: since Llama's release, anyone can run powerful models locally.
terms.example_en:
· 2023: Llama 2 open-sourced for commercial use → Late 2023: Mistral MoE → 2024: Llama 3 closely trails GPT-4.
· Value: Zero API costs, zero data leakage, and fine-tuning for specialized models.
· Challenges: Requires GPUs, demands operational overhead, and risks rapid obsolescence.
· Selection criteria: Benchmark scores, hardware requirements, and Chinese capabilities (DeepSeek and Qwen excel here).
examples_en: 2023: Llama 2 open-sourced for commercial use → Late 2023: Mistral MoE → 2024: Llama 3 closely trails GPT-4.
Value: Zero API costs, zero data leakage, and fine-tuning for specialized models.
Challenges: Requires GPUs, demands operational overhead, and risks rapid obsolescence.
Selection criteria: Benchmark scores, hardware requirements, and Chinese capabilities (DeepSeek and Qwen excel here).

terms.definition_short: P 值是统计学里的"犯傻概率"——在虚无假设成立的前提下，看到当前数据或更极端数据的概率，常用于 A/B 测试判断提升是否真实。
terms.definition_short_en: A P-value is the probability of observing the current or more extreme data assuming the null hypothesis is true, commonly used in A/B testing to determine if an improvement is real.

terms.definition_short: PagedAttention 把 KV Cache 切成固定大小的页，用链接表管理，不要求连续存放，是 LLM 推理效率的关键突破。
terms.definition_short_en: PagedAttention divides the KV Cache into fixed-size pages managed by a linked table, eliminating the need for contiguous memory allocation and marking a key breakthrough in LLM inference efficiency.

terms.definition_short: PDP 强调认知由大量简单单元并行协作产生，知识分布在连接权重中，是连接主义和神经网络复兴的理论背景。
terms.definition_short_en: Parallel Distributed Processing (PDP) emphasizes that cognition emerges from the parallel collaboration of many simple units, with knowledge distributed across connection weights, serving as the theoretical foundation for the revival of connectionism and neural networks.

terms.definition_short: 感知机是单层二分类器，只能判线性可分的事，是深度学习的种子。
terms.definition_short_en: A perceptron is a single-layer binary classifier limited to linearly separable problems, serving as the foundational seed of modern deep learning.

terms.definition_short: PSSH 认为智能可以通过符号操作实现，是符号主义 AI 的理论基石，支撑了逻辑推理、问题求解、专家系统和知识表示。
terms.definition_short_en: PSSH posits that intelligence can be achieved through symbol manipulation. As the theoretical cornerstone of symbolic AI, it underpinned logical reasoning, problem-solving, expert systems, and knowledge representation.

terms.definition_short: PR 曲线是精确率-召回率曲线，AUC-PR 是曲线下面积，在不平衡数据上比 AUC-ROC 更有信息量。
terms.definition_short_en: A Precision-Recall (PR) curve plots precision against recall, and AUC-PR represents the area under this curve. It provides a more informative performance metric than AUC-ROC for highly imbalanced datasets.

terms.definition_short: 产生式系统用 if-then 规则构建知识库，推理引擎根据当前事实匹配规则并执行，是早期符号 AI 的核心技术。
terms.definition_short_en: A production system builds a knowledge base using if-then rules, which an inference engine matches and executes based on current facts, serving as the core technology of early symbolic AI.
terms.back_en: The fundamental mechanism of AI systems that encodes knowledge using rules like "if condition A is met, then execute action B." An inference engine matches and executes these rules based on current facts, serving as the technical foundation of expert systems.
terms.definition_long_en:
The fundamental idea behind production systems is simple yet powerful: knowledge is encoded as individual "if-then" rules, and an inference engine matches and executes them based on current facts. These are known as "production rules."

This mechanism flourished during the era of expert systems. In 1977, numerous similar systems emerged, building on the early work of Dendral. Stanford University's Mycin system utilized an inference engine based on if-then logic, paired with a knowledge base of approximately 600 rules, specifically designed to diagnose blood infections. By inputting patient symptoms, the system matched rules to infer potential pathogens and provide medication recommendations.

In the 1980s, production systems were commercialized. Early AI companies like Teknowledge packaged this technology into workstations and sold them to enterprises. However, critics pointed out that these systems were "nothing more than a bunch of if-then-else statements strung together and packaged in an overpriced workstation." This highlighted both the ubiquity and the limitations of production systems—simply piling up rules does not equate to true intelligence. Once the number of rules exploded, maintenance costs became prohibitively high, and the systems remained incapable of handling novel situations not covered by existing rules.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Production systems serve as the technical foundation of expert systems. The concept of encoding knowledge with if-then rules is simple yet powerful, but its limitations also foreshadowed the boundaries of symbolic AI—simply piling up rules does not equate to intelligence.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the "if-then" building blocks of expert systems, where piling up too many rules causes maintenance costs to explode.
terms.example_en:
· The Mycin system used about 600 if-then rules to reason about blood infections and recommend medications.
· In the 1980s, Teknowledge packaged production systems into workstations to sell to enterprises.
· Limitation: Maintenance costs skyrocket after a rule explosion, and the system cannot handle novel situations not covered by existing rules.
examples_en:
The core mechanism of AI systems built with "if-then" rules, where an inference engine matches and executes corresponding rules based on current facts.

Production systems are the technical foundation of expert systems, and their core idea is simple yet powerful: using "if condition A is met

terms.term_zh: 召回率 vs 精确率
terms.definition_short: 召回率与精确率是分类模型两个方向相反的指标，医疗诊断要召回率高（不漏诊），垃圾邮件过滤要精确率高（不错杀）。
terms.definition_short_en: Recall and precision are inversely related metrics in classification models. Medical diagnoses prioritize high recall to avoid missing cases, while spam filtering prioritizes high precision to avoid misclassifying legitimate emails.
terms.displayName: 召回率 vs 精确率

terms.definition_short: 感受野是视觉系统中每个神经元所对应的视野区域，单个神经元只对这一小块区域里的视觉刺激作出反应。
terms.definition_short_en: A receptive field is the specific region of the visual field associated with an individual neuron, which only responds to visual stimuli within this small area.

terms.definition_short: RL 基础是强化学习的底层框架，Agent 在环境里通过试错最大化累积奖励，分价值函数和策略函数两大路线。
terms.definition_short_en: The foundational framework of reinforcement learning involves an agent maximizing cumulative rewards through trial and error in an environment, primarily divided into value-based and policy-based approaches.
terms.front_en: What are the basics of Reinforcement Learning?
terms.back_en: Think of training a dog: hearing a command (state) → choosing to sit (action) → getting a treat (reward) → repeating until learned. These are RL's five elements: agent, environment, state, action, and reward.
terms.definition_long_en:
Reinforcement learning is the underlying framework for AI to learn through trial and error. Its five core elements are: an agent (the learner) observes the current state within an environment, selects an action, and the environment returns a reward and a new state—repeating this cycle. The agent's goal is to maximize cumulative rewards, rather than just the reward for a single step.

The most intuitive example is training a dog. The dog hears a command (state), chooses to sit, run, or eat (action), and either gets a treat or doesn't (reward). After multiple repetitions, it learns to sit when hearing the command. AlphaGo used this framework to master Go, and ChatGPT uses it to learn how to generate satisfactory responses.

There are two main approaches. Value-based methods learn how good each state or state-action pair is—essentially evaluating if a state is worth being in. Q-learning and DQN are representative algorithms. Policy-based methods directly learn which action to take in each state without evaluating its underlying value. Policy Gradient and PPO are prime examples.

The fundamental difference between RL and supervised learning lies here: supervised learning provides correct answers (e.g., "this image is a cat"), whereas RL only provides reward signals (e.g., "this step scored points") without a standard answer key. The agent must discover which actions yield rewards through trial and error—much like a toddler learning to walk by stumbling and falling until they figure it out themselves.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Reinforcement learning is the framework that enables AI to learn autonomously through trial and error. Its five core elements—agent, environment, state, action, and reward—form the underlying logic for everything from AlphaGo's gameplay to ChatGPT's alignment training.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the mathematical version of training a dog: state, action, reward, and trial-and-error until learned, aiming for cumulative rewards.
terms.example_en:
· Five elements: An agent observes a state in an environment and selects an action → the environment returns a reward and a new state → repeat.
· Value functions learn how good each state is (Q-learning/DQN), while policy functions directly learn which action to take (PPO).
· Fundamental difference from supervised learning: No correct answers, only reward signals—learning through trial and error.
· A classic beginner task is running CartPole (OpenAI Gym/Gymnasium); the DQN paper is a major milestone.
examples_en: Five elements: An agent observes a state in an environment and selects an action → the environment returns a reward and a new state → repeat. The goal is cumulative, not single-step, rewards.
Value functions learn how good each state is (Q-learning/DQN), while policy functions directly learn which action to take (PPO).
The fundamental difference from supervised learning: there are no correct answers, only reward signals—discovered through trial and error. A toddler learning to walk is a classic RL analogy.
A classic beginner task is running CartPole in OpenAI Gym. The DQN paper stands as a major milestone.

terms.definition_short: 环境交互学习强调 Agent 通过与环境持续交互、从反馈中学习，是强化学习的根本范式。
terms.definition_short_en: RL from Environment is the fundamental paradigm of reinforcement learning, emphasizing that an agent learns through continuous interaction with its environment and adapting based on the resulting feedback.

terms.definition_short: RL for LLM 是强化学习在大语言模型里的新应用，涵盖对齐（RLHF/DPO）、推理（o1/R1）、Agent（Claude Code）三个方向。
terms.definition_short_en: RL for LLM represents the application of reinforcement learning to large language models, focusing on three primary directions: alignment (RLHF/DPO), reasoning (o1/R1), and AI agents (Claude Code).

terms.definition_short: RNN 是基础循环网络，序列长了梯度消失记不住；LSTM 1997 年加门控机制解决长程依赖，是 RNN 到 Transformer 之间的过渡。
terms.definition_short_en: RNNs are basic recurrent networks that suffer from vanishing gradients on long sequences. Introduced in 1997, LSTMs added gating mechanisms to solve long-range dependencies, serving as the dominant architecture before Transformers.

terms.definition_short: RNN vs Transformer 是两个序列模型的代际对比，Transformer 用注意力替代了 RNN 的按序传递，从 2017 年起统一了 NLP。
terms.definition_short_en: RNN vs Transformer compares two generations of sequence models. By replacing the sequential processing of RNNs with attention mechanisms, Transformers have unified natural language processing since 2017.

terms.definition_short: 机器人学研究机器的感知、决策和行动能力，从早期 Shakey 到现代自动驾驶，是 AI 走向物理世界的桥梁。
terms.definition_short_en: Robotics studies the perception, decision-making, and action capabilities of machines. Spanning from the early Shakey robot to modern autonomous driving, it serves as the bridge for AI to enter the physical world.

terms.definition_short: Scaling Law 是大模型能力随数据、参数和计算量增加而提升的经验规律，服从幂律关系，有最优配比。
terms.definition_short_en: Scaling laws are empirical rules describing how a foundation model's capabilities improve as data, parameters, and compute increase, following a power-law relationship with an optimal allocation ratio.

terms.definition_short: Scaling Law 深层涵盖计算最优配比、推理时扩展、数据墙与合成数据等细分方向，是 scaling 研究的前沿。
terms.definition_short_en: The deeper dimensions of Scaling Laws encompass compute-optimal ratios, inference-time scaling, the data wall, and synthetic data, representing the current frontier of scaling research.

terms.definition_short: 视觉 Scaling Law 指图像模型也遵循规模定律，ViT 的参数、数据、计算越大效果越好，2023 年被正式确认。
terms.definition_short_en: The Vision Scaling Law states that image models also follow scaling principles: performance improves as parameters, data, and compute increase. Formally confirmed in 2023, it validated this approach for architectures like ViT.

terms.definition_short: SCAN 用结构化状态空间对偶性，把 Mamba 和 RWKV 统一到同一个框架，是序列架构走向统一化的理论尝试。
terms.definition_short_en: SCAN uses structured state space duality to unify Mamba and RWKV into a single framework, representing a theoretical attempt to standardize sequence architectures.

terms.definition_short: 自注意力是 Transformer 的根本机制，句子内每个词跟所有词打分计算关联，所有 token 两两算关系，并行全图。
terms.definition_short_en: Self-attention is the fundamental mechanism of the Transformer, where every token in a sentence calculates an association score with all other tokens in parallel to capture global relationships.

terms.definition_short: 可分离卷积把标准卷积分解成深度级和逐点两步，省计算，是移动端 AI 的数学工具。
terms.definition_short_en: Separable convolution breaks down standard convolution into depthwise and pointwise steps to save computation, serving as a core mathematical tool for mobile AI.

terms.definition_short: 脚本是 Schank 提出的知识结构，描述事件发生的标准情景，让 AI 能理解故事中隐含的常识。
terms.definition_short_en: Proposed by Roger Schank, scripts are knowledge structures that describe standard event sequences, enabling AI systems to grasp the implicit common sense embedded in stories.

terms.definition_short: SLAM 是机器人同时进行自定位和地图构建的技术，由 Sebastian Thrun 等人在 20 世纪 90 年代推向实用。
terms.definition_short_en: SLAM is the technology that enables robots to simultaneously localize themselves and map their surroundings, brought into practical use by Sebastian Thrun and others in the 1990s.

terms.definition_short: 滑动窗口注意力是长序列注意力的节省技巧——每个词只看周围 K 个词，靠多层堆叠把远距信息逐层传开。
terms.definition_short_en: Sliding Window Attention is an efficiency technique for long sequences where each token only attends to its K nearest neighbors, relying on multiple stacked layers to propagate long-distance information step-by-step.

terms.definition_short: 稀疏自编码器在隐藏层加稀疏性约束，强制每个样本只激活少数神经元，让特征分开而非纠缠。
terms.definition_short_en: A sparse autoencoder applies a sparsity constraint to its hidden layer, forcing only a small number of neurons to activate per sample to disentangle features and make them individually interpretable.

terms.definition_short: 流式 LLM 让模型逐 token 实时输出，而非等全部算完再显示，降低用户感知延迟。
terms.definition_short_en: Streaming LLMs output text token by token in real time rather than waiting for the entire computation to finish, significantly reducing perceived latency for the user.

terms.definition_short: 强 AI 主张机器能真正思考和拥有心智，弱 AI 主张机器只是模拟智能行为——这是 AI 哲学的根本分歧。
terms.definition_short_en: Strong AI asserts that machines can truly think and possess a mind, whereas Weak AI argues they merely simulate intelligent behavior—a fundamental divide in AI philosophy.

terms.definition_short: 符号主义用规则和逻辑模拟智能，联结主义用神经网络模拟大脑——是 AI 史上两条根本对立路线。
terms.definition_short_en: Symbolism simulates intelligence using rules and logic, while Connectionism simulates the brain using neural networks, representing two fundamentally opposing paths in the history of AI.

terms.definition_short: Trajectory Transformer 是 2021 年 Berkeley 提出的离线强化学习模型，把序列决策转成序列建模问题。
terms.definition_short_en: Proposed by UC Berkeley in 2021, the Trajectory Transformer is an offline reinforcement learning model that frames sequential decision-making as a sequence modeling problem.

terms.definition_short: Transformer Block 是 Transformer 的基本单元，由自注意力、残差连接、层归一化、前馈网络四步组成。
terms.definition_short_en: The Transformer Block is the fundamental building block of a Transformer model, consisting of four main operations: self-attention, residual connections, layer normalization, and a feed-forward network.

terms.definition_short: Transformer 家族分为 Encoder-Only、Decoder-Only、Encoder-Decoder 三种架构分支，代表是 BERT、GPT、T5。
terms.definition_short_en: The Transformer family consists of three main architectural branches: encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder, with BERT, GPT, and T5 serving as their respective representatives.

terms.definition_short: Transformer-XL 是 2019 年 Google 和 CMU 提出的长文本 Transformer，用段际记忆回环打破固定长度限制。
terms.definition_short_en: Proposed by Google and CMU in 2019, Transformer-XL is an architecture designed for long texts that breaks fixed-length constraints using a segment-level recurrence mechanism.

terms.definition_short: Transformers 库是 HuggingFace 的模型库——几行 Python 代码加载和运行几万个 AI 模型。
terms.definition_short_en: The Transformers library is Hugging Face's flagship model library, allowing developers to load and run tens of thousands of AI models with just a few lines of Python code.

terms.definition_short: 基本收入（UBI）是政府向每位公民无差别发放固定现金的政策方案，被视为应对 AI 技术性失业的可能解。
terms.definition_short_en: Universal Basic Income (UBI) is a policy proposal where the government unconditionally distributes a fixed amount of cash to every citizen, viewed as a potential solution to AI-induced technological unemployment.

terms.definition_short: 无监督学习是数据没有标签的学习范式，让模型自己发现结构、分群、降维、找规律。
terms.definition_short_en: Unsupervised learning is a paradigm that uses unlabeled data, allowing the model to independently discover underlying structures, cluster information, reduce dimensionality, and find patterns.

terms.definition_short: 权重共享是多个位置或任务使用同一组参数——CNN 共享空间参数，RNN 共享时间参数，孪生网络共享对比参数。
terms.definition_short_en: Weight sharing is the use of the same set of parameters across multiple positions or tasks—CNNs share parameters spatially, RNNs share them temporally, and Siamese networks share them for contrastive tasks.

terms.definition_short: 词嵌入把词变成向量，让意思相近的词在空间里距离更近，是 NLP 从符号文字走向可计算语义的关键一步。
terms.definition_short_en: Word embedding transforms words into vectors, placing semantically similar words closer together in space. It marks a critical step in NLP's transition from symbolic text to computable semantics.

terms.definition_short: 万维网（WWW）是用 URL、HTML、HTTP 和超链接把网页连成全球信息网络的基础设施。
terms.definition_short_en: The World Wide Web (WWW) is the infrastructure that uses URLs, HTML, HTTP, and hyperlinks to connect web pages into a global information network.

terms.definition_short: YOLO vs R-CNN 是目标检测的两代——R-CNN 两阶段先提议再分类准但慢，YOLO 单阶段一次出所有框快但早期精度不够。
terms.definition_short_en: YOLO and R-CNN represent two paradigms in object detection: R-CNN's two-stage approach (propose then classify) is accurate but slow, while YOLO's single-stage approach outputs all bounding boxes at once—extremely fast, though early versions struggled with accuracy.

terms.definition_short: 强化学习让智能体在行动和反馈里学习——做得好给奖励，做得差就调整，是理解 Agent、游戏 AI、机器人和 RLHF 的基础概念。
terms.definition_short_en: Reinforcement learning enables AI agents to learn through actions and feedback—earning rewards for good choices and adjusting after bad ones. It is foundational for understanding agents, game AI, robotics, and RLHF.

terms.definition_short: AI vs IA 是同一个技术的两个方向——让机器取代你（AI），还是让机器帮你变得更厉害（IA）。
terms.definition_short_en: AI vs IA represents two divergent paths of the same technology: building machines to replace human labor (Artificial Intelligence) versus building machines to augment human capabilities (Intelligence Amplification).

terms.definition_short: 对齐税是让 AI 变得更安全更听话所付出的代价——对齐越好的模型往往越拒绝回答、越保守、越无聊。
terms.definition_short_en: The alignment tax is the cost of making an AI safer and more compliant. Highly aligned models often become more prone to refusals, overly conservative, and ultimately more boring.

terms.definition_short: AGI（通用人工智能）是能执行人类可以完成的任何智力任务的 AI，区别于只擅长单一任务的窄 AI。
terms.definition_short_en: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is an AI capable of performing any intellectual task that a human can do, distinguishing it from narrow AI that excels only at single tasks.

terms.definition_short: 李飞飞用 5.4 亿年前视觉引发生物大爆发来类比计算机视觉可能驱动 AI 智能的爆发式增长。
terms.definition_short_en: Fei-Fei Li uses the Cambrian Explosion—where the emergence of vision 540 million years ago triggered massive biological diversity—as a metaphor for how computer vision could drive explosive growth in AI intelligence.

terms.definition_short: 中文屋是 John Searle 1980 年提出的思想实验——用来反驳强 AI"机器能真正思考"的主张。
terms.definition_short_en: The Chinese Room is a thought experiment proposed by John Searle in 1980 to refute the strong AI claim that machines can truly think.

terms.definition_short: 计算创造力研究 AI 能否以及如何表现出创造行为，从生成图到写诗——核心争议是 AI 的创造是真正创新还是对训练数据的统计重组。
terms.definition_short_en: Computational creativity studies whether and how AI can exhibit creative behaviors, from generating images to writing poetry. The core debate is whether AI's creations represent genuine innovation or merely the statistical recombination of its training data.

terms.definition_short: 内容审核 AI 用深度学习和 NLP 自动检测 UGC 平台上的违规内容，是社交媒体和平台的第一道防线。
terms.definition_short_en: AI content moderation uses deep learning and NLP to automatically detect policy violations on user-generated content (UGC) platforms, serving as the first line of defense for social media.

terms.term_zh: 交叉编码器 vs 双编码器
terms.definition_short: 交叉编码器 vs 双编码器是语义搜索的两种根本编码策略——双编码器独立编码快但粗略，交叉编码器拼在一起慢但精准。
terms.definition_short_en: Cross-Encoders and Bi-Encoders are two fundamental encoding strategies in semantic search: Bi-Encoders encode independently for fast but rough retrieval, while Cross-Encoders process inputs together for slow but highly accurate results.
terms.displayName: 交叉编码器 vs 双编码器

terms.definition_short: 跨模态学习是 AI 在不同感官模态之间建立映射和推理的能力——从一种模态生成另一种。
terms.definition_short_en: Cross-modal learning is the ability of AI to establish mappings and reason across different sensory modalities, enabling it to generate content in one modality from another.

terms.definition_short: AI 网络安全关注 AI 系统特有的攻击面——对抗样本、提示注入、模型窃取等，是对模型从训练到部署全链路的保护。
terms.definition_short_en: AI cybersecurity focuses on attack surfaces unique to AI systems—such as adversarial examples, prompt injection, and model stealing—providing full-lifecycle protection for models from training to deployment.

terms.definition_short: 道格拉斯·恩格尔巴特是 1960 年代提出用计算机增强人类智能（IA 路线）的先驱——发明了鼠标、超文本、视频会议。
terms.definition_short_en: Douglas Engelbart was a 1960s pioneer who advocated using computers to augment human intelligence (the IA approach), inventing the computer mouse, hypertext, and video conferencing along the way.

terms.definition_short: 具身智能认为 AI 应该拥有身体并生活在物理世界里，在真实世界中行动、感知和互动，而非只存在于屏幕上的文字。
terms.definition_short_en: Embodied intelligence posits that AI should possess a physical body and inhabit the real world, acting, perceiving, and interacting with its environment, rather than existing merely as text on a screen.

terms.definition_short: 能量模型通过为每个输入或输入-输出对分配一个能量值来建模——能量越低代表越可能是真答案。
terms.definition_short_en: An Energy-Based Model works by assigning an energy value to each input or input-output pair, where lower energy indicates a higher likelihood of being the correct answer.

terms.definition_short: 基础模型是在大规模数据上预训练出来的通用 AI 模型，掌握了语言或视觉的基本规律后，可以通过微调适应各种具体任务。
terms.definition_short_en: A foundation model is a general-purpose AI model pre-trained on massive data that, having mastered the basic patterns of language or vision, can be fine-tuned for various specific tasks.

terms.term_zh: 生成式 vs 判别式
terms.definition_short: 生成式 vs 判别式是 AI 建模的两种根本思路——判别式只学边界，生成式学整体分布。
terms.definition_short_en: Generative and discriminative modeling are two fundamental approaches in AI: discriminative models only learn boundaries between classes, while generative models learn the overall distribution of the data.
terms.displayName: 生成式 vs 判别式

terms.definition_short: GLM-5.2 是智谱 AI 2026 年发布的旗舰基座模型，定位是长程任务时代的底座。
terms.definition_short_en: GLM-5.2 is Zhipu AI's flagship foundation model released in 2026, positioned as a foundation for the era of long-horizon tasks.

terms.definition_short: GPT Store 是 OpenAI 2024 年推出的 GPT 应用市场，任何人都能做一个定制版 ChatGPT 发布出去给人用，不需要写代码。
terms.definition_short_en: The GPT Store is an application marketplace launched by OpenAI in 2024, allowing anyone to create and publish a customized version of ChatGPT for others to use without writing any code.

terms.definition_short: Groq LPU（Language Processing Unit）是专门为语言模型推理设计的芯片，跟通用 GPU 走完全不同的路线。
terms.definition_short_en: The Groq LPU (Language Processing Unit) is a custom chip designed specifically for language model inference, taking a completely different architectural approach from general-purpose GPUs.

terms.definition_short: 人类评估是用人而非自动指标来评判 AI 的输出质量，是 RLHF 的根本环节，因为很多 AI 输出的好坏无法用机器打分。
terms.definition_short_en: Human evaluation uses human raters rather than automated metrics to judge the quality of AI outputs. It is a fundamental component of RLHF, as machines cannot adequately score many subjective aspects of AI generation.

terms.definition_short: 超文本是通过链接把不同文档连接起来的文本形式——点一下就能跳到另一页，是万维网的细胞。
terms.definition_short_en: Hypertext is a text format that connects different documents through hyperlinks. It allows users to jump from one page to another with a single click, serving as the fundamental building block of the World Wide Web.

terms.definition_short: MLOps 把机器学习从实验室的一次性实验变成可复现、可监控、可持续运行的生产线——借鉴 DevOps 理念但更复杂。
terms.definition_short_en: MLOps transforms machine learning from one-off laboratory experiments into reproducible, monitorable, and sustainable production pipelines—borrowing concepts from DevOps but adding significantly more complexity.

terms.definition_short: 机器遗忘是让训练好的 AI 模型移除特定训练数据影响的技术——从模型参数中撤销特定数据的影响，而非删文件。
terms.definition_short_en: Machine unlearning is a technique that enables a trained AI model to remove the influence of specific training data—undoing its effect on the model's parameters rather than simply deleting a file.

terms.definition_short: 窄 AI 是今天你用的所有 AI 的实际形态——只能做一件事但能把这件事做到极致，跟 AGI 相对。
terms.definition_short_en: Narrow AI represents the actual state of all AI you use today—systems designed to do one specific thing exceptionally well, standing in contrast to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI).

terms.definition_short: NAS 是神经架构搜索——让 AI 自己设计更好的 AI 架构。
terms.definition_short_en: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is a technique that automates the design of artificial neural networks, effectively using AI to design better AI architectures.

terms.definition_short: 个人电脑是把计算机从机房搬到桌面的关键一步，是人类计算能力大规模普及的基础设施。
terms.definition_short_en: The personal computer was the critical step in moving computing from server rooms to desktops, serving as the foundational infrastructure that democratized computing power for the masses.

terms.definition_short: Pipeline 是 AI 工程里的流水线——数据从原始状态经过清洗、训练、评估、部署，每一站都有专门的组件，像工厂的装配线。
terms.definition_short_en: A Pipeline is the assembly line of AI engineering. Raw data moves through cleaning, training, evaluation, and deployment, with specialized components handling each station just like a factory floor.

terms.definition_short: 搜索增强生成是 RAG 的近亲——让 AI 在回答问题过程中主动上网搜索、查数据库、调用工具，像人做研究一样边查边写。
terms.definition_short_en: A close relative of RAG, Search Augmented Generation allows an AI to actively search the web, query databases, and use tools mid-response, researching and writing simultaneously like a human researcher.

terms.definition_short: Tesla Optimus 是特斯拉 2022 年发布的人形机器人——身高约一米七，重约六十公斤，用自动驾驶的视觉和 AI 系统做感知和决策。
terms.definition_short_en: Tesla Optimus is a humanoid robot unveiled in 2022. Standing about 1.7 meters tall and weighing around 60 kilograms, it leverages Tesla's autonomous driving vision and AI systems for perception and decision-making.

terms.definition_short: 推理时计算让 AI 在回答问题之前花额外的计算资源来思考，就像人在考试时先在草稿纸上演算。
terms.definition_short_en: Test-time compute allows AI to spend additional computational resources thinking before answering a question, much like a person using scratch paper during an exam.

terms.definition_short: Transformer 架构是 2017 年提出的神经网络架构，用自注意力取代了 RNN 的循环结构——一次性让每个词看所有词。GPT、BERT、LLaMA、Stable Diffusion 的心脏都是它。
terms.definition_short_en: Introduced in 2017, the Transformer is a neural network architecture that replaces sequential RNNs with self-attention, allowing every word to process all other words simultaneously. It serves as the core engine for GPT, BERT, LLaMA, and Stable Diffusion.
terms.back_en: RNNs read sequentially and often forget the beginning. Transformers process all words simultaneously, allowing each word to calculate its relationship with every other word. This parallel processing drastically accelerates training and enables models to understand much longer contexts.
terms.definition_long_en:
The Transformer architecture was introduced by Google in the landmark 2017 paper *Attention Is All You Need*.

Its core innovation is the self-attention mechanism, which allows the representation of each position in a sequence to aggregate global information by calculating attention weights with all other positions simultaneously. This solved two fundamental problems of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs): the inability to parallelize sequential processing, which made training slow, and the loss of long-range dependencies due to vanishing gradients in long sequences.

The architecture consists of an encoder and a decoder. Each layer contains multi-head self-attention and feed-forward networks, stabilized by residual connections and layer normalization. By discarding all recurrences and convolutions in favor of pure attention, this design transformed the entire AI field. GPT uses it for text generation, BERT for text understanding, ViT for image classification, and Stable Diffusion embeds self-attention within its U-Net backbone.

Years later, nearly all frontier AI models are descendants of the Transformer.
terms.why_it_matters_en: The Transformer is the universal engine of modern AI. From chatbots and image generation to protein folding, this architecture powers the underlying technology. Understanding the Transformer is essential to understanding how contemporary AI works.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as a massive conference where every word talks to all other words simultaneously instead of waiting in line to speak.
terms.example_en:
· A 2017 eight-page paper discarded RNNs to replace everything with self-attention, letting every word look at all other words simultaneously.
· Training became highly parallelized and exponentially faster, while long contexts no longer suffered from forgetting the beginning.
· GPT, BERT, LLaMA, ViT, and Stable Diffusion are all descendants of the Transformer.
examples_en: A 2017 eight-page paper discarded RNNs to replace everything with self-attention, letting every word look at all other words simultaneously, which made training highly parallelized and exponentially faster without forgetting the beginning of long contexts.
GPT, BERT, LLaMA, ViT, and Stable Diffusion are all descendants of the Transformer, an architecture that transformed the entire AI field over the past seven years.

terms.definition_short: 手推车难题是英国哲学家菲利帕·福特 1967 年提出的经典伦理思想实验——一辆失控的电车冲向五个被绑在轨道上的人，你拉一下拉杆电车会变轨，但另一条轨道上绑着一个人。
terms.definition_short_en: Introduced by British philosopher Philippa Foot in 1967, the Trolley Problem is a classic ethical thought experiment: a runaway trolley hurtles toward five people, but pulling a lever diverts it to kill only one.

terms.definition_short: 视觉要点是大脑在 27 毫秒内把握场景整体意义的能力——你不需要先认出桌子再认出人在吃饭，你一眼就抓到了整个场景的要点。
terms.definition_short_en: Visual gist is the brain's ability to grasp a scene's overall meaning in just 27 milliseconds. Instead of recognizing individual objects sequentially, you instantly comprehend the entire scene at a glance.

terms.definition_short: Waymo 是 Google/Alphabet 的自动驾驶公司——2009 年起源于 Google 无人车项目，2016 年独立。
