terms.definition_short_en: Karpathy is widely regarded as the educator who introduced many to the field of AI—he is the creator of nanoGPT and the originator of the term "vibe coding."
terms.back_en: A founding research scientist at OpenAI, former Director of AI at Tesla, and creator of nanoGPT. He is widely known as the educator who introduced many to AI, coined "vibe coding" in 2025, and joined Anthropic's pretraining team in 2026.
terms.definition_long_en:
Andrej Karpathy is widely regarded as the educator who introduced many to the field of AI. He was a founding research scientist at OpenAI, joining on its very first day in 2015, and served as one of the foundational figures behind the GPT trajectory that later transformed the industry.

He is celebrated for his educational contributions, notably writing nanoGPT—a minimalist 300-line code implementation designed for teaching. His "Zero to Hero" YouTube series, which builds a GPT from scratch line by line, is considered a definitive guide for AI self-study. He also served as the primary instructor for Stanford's CS231n (Deep Learning for Computer Vision), a course that grew from 150 students in 2015 to 750 in 2017 and became a standard global curriculum for AI education.

Beyond research and teaching, Karpathy is a leading practitioner of applied AI engineering. From 2017 to 2022, he served as the Director of AI at Tesla, leading the Autopilot vision system and advancing the pure-vision approach to autonomous driving. In 2024, he founded Eureka Labs, launching LLM101n as its first product. He coined the term "vibe coding" in February 2025 to describe collaborative programming with AI using natural language, and in May 2026, he joined Anthropic to lead its pretraining team.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Understanding deep learning, Transformers, and GPT training mechanisms often begins with Karpathy's educational materials. Grasping frontier model development methodologies starts with his insights on extrapolation and scaling loss. He is among the rare few who have successfully bridged research, teaching, product engineering, and entrepreneurship.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember him as the educator who introduced the world to AI—creator of nanoGPT, the "Zero to Hero" series, and vibe coding.
terms.example_en:
· Joined OpenAI on its first day in 2015 as a founding research scientist.
  · Served as Director of AI at Tesla from 2017 to 2022, leading Autopilot vision.
  · Founded Eureka Labs in 2024, launching LLM101n as its first product.
  · Coined "vibe coding" on X in February 2025, which Collins Dictionary named its 2025 Word of the Year.
  · Announced on X on May 19, 2026, that he was joining Anthropic to lead the pretraining team.
examples_en: Joined OpenAI on its first day in 2015 as a founding research scientist.
Served as Director of AI at Tesla from 2017 to 2022, leading Autopilot vision.
Founded Eureka Labs in 2024, launching LLM101n as its first product.
Coined "vibe coding" on X in February 2025, which Collins Dictionary named its 2025 Word of the Year.
Announced on X on May 19, 2026, that he was joining Anthropic to lead the pretraining team.

terms.definition_short: Andrew Ng 是把机器学习课开给全世界的那个人。
terms.definition_short_en: Andrew Ng is the pioneering educator and researcher who brought machine learning courses to a global audience.

terms.definition_short: Anthropic：2021 年从 OpenAI 出走的创始人 Dario Amodei 创立——以 AI 安全对齐为根本使命。
terms.definition_short_en: Founded in 2021 by Dario Amodei after departing OpenAI, Anthropic is an AI company whose fundamental mission is AI safety and alignment.
terms.back_en: An AI company founded in 2021 by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei after leaving OpenAI. Its core mission is AI safety and alignment, and its Claude models are the primary competitors to GPT.
terms.definition_long_en:
What is Anthropic? It is the leading advocate for the AI safety approach.

In 2021, siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei left OpenAI to found Anthropic. They publicly stated their reason for leaving: they felt OpenAI was underinvesting in AI safety during its commercialization and were dissatisfied with its shift to a "capped-profit" structure. Anthropic's core mission is not to build the most powerful AI, but the safest.

The company's safety research contributions include Constitutional AI, which uses written principles for model self-critique rather than relying solely on human preferences; systematic red-teaming, where a full-time safety team continuously attacks Claude to find vulnerabilities; and its Responsible Scaling Policy, which defines safety measures based on model capability levels (one of the industry's earliest capability-tiered safety frameworks).

In 2024, Claude 3.5 Sonnet surpassed GPT-4 on multiple benchmarks, and Claude Code earned a stronger reputation in the developer community than Copilot. By 2025, Amazon had invested a cumulative $8 billion in the company. Anthropic is deeply integrated with AWS, conducting its training primarily on AWS Trainium chips. Google has also invested approximately $2 billion.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Anthropic represents a distinct path in AI development: prioritizing an AI that remains harmless as it grows more capable, rather than simply pursuing maximum power. Its rivalry with OpenAI essentially embodies the competition between two AI philosophies: speed versus safety.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the antithesis of OpenAI: competing on safety rather than raw power.
terms.example_en:
· In 2021, the Amodei siblings left OpenAI to found Anthropic because they felt OpenAI was underinvesting in safety.
· Safety contributions: Constitutional AI for principle-based critique, systematic red-teaming, and the Responsible Scaling Policy.
· In 2024, Claude 3.5 surpassed GPT-4 on multiple benchmarks, and Claude Code outperformed Copilot in developer community reputation.
· OpenAI pursues speed and capability, while Anthropic pursues safety and control—representing two distinct paths in AI development.
examples_en: In 2021, the Amodei siblings left OpenAI to found Anthropic because they felt OpenAI was underinvesting in safety.
Safety contributions: Constitutional AI for principle-based critique, systematic red-teaming, and the Responsible Scaling Policy.
In 2024, Claude 3.5 surpassed GPT-4 on multiple benchmarks, and Claude Code outperformed Copilot in developer community reputation.
OpenAI pursues speed and capability, while Anthropic pursues safety and control—representing two distinct paths in AI development.

terms.definition_short: Anthropic 安全研究：不仅仅是 RLHF——Constitutional AI、对齐伪装研究、可解释性研究的完整安全研究栈。
terms.definition_short_en: Anthropic Safety Research goes beyond RLHF, offering a complete safety stack that includes Constitutional AI, deceptive alignment studies, and mechanistic interpretability.

terms.definition_short: 苹果不是 AI 论文最多的公司，但通过硬件和操作系统把 AI 嵌入了数十亿台设备。
terms.definition_short_en: While not the most prolific publisher of AI research, Apple has successfully embedded AI into billions of devices through its hardware and operating systems.
terms.front_en: How is Apple connected to AI?
terms.back_en: Since acquiring Siri in 2010, Apple has continuously embedded AI into its hardware and operating systems. Through A-series chips with Neural Engines, Core ML, and the Vision framework, Apple has brought AI to billions of devices.
terms.definition_long_en:
Apple's AI roadmap differs from pure AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic—it focuses on building the most private AI rather than the most powerful models.

Since acquiring the Siri voice assistant in 2010, Apple has continuously embedded AI into its hardware and operating systems. Its A-series chips (starting with the A11 in 2017) feature built-in Neural Engines capable of processing trillions of AI operations per second. Core ML allows developers to seamlessly deploy models to the iPhone, iPad, and Mac; the Vision framework handles real-time image understanding; and the Natural Language framework performs language analysis.

Apple's AI philosophy prioritizes privacy, historically processing data on-device rather than uploading it to the cloud. This approach shifted slightly with the 2024 introduction of Apple Intelligence: simple tasks remain on-device, while complex tasks are routed to the cloud (Private Cloud Compute). However, Apple emphasizes that this cloud processing is encrypted and data is immediately discarded after use.

At WWDC 2024, Apple announced Apple Intelligence, partnering with OpenAI to integrate ChatGPT into iOS 18 while also developing its own small on-device models. This marked Apple's official entry into the generative AI race, though its strategy remains focused on using AI to enhance hardware experiences rather than offering AI as a standalone product.
terms.why_it_matters_en: While Apple may not publish the most AI research papers, Siri, Neural Engine chips, and Core ML have brought AI to billions of devices—an impact no single paper can achieve. It represents an alternative path to AI democratization: through hardware rather than APIs.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the company that packed AI into billions of iPhones, prioritizing privacy and on-device processing.
terms.example_en:
· Siri was the world's first widely commercialized AI voice assistant (launched with the iPhone 4S in 2011).
· The iPhone's Neural Engine can process trillions of AI operations per second.
· Core ML allows developers to seamlessly deploy models to the iPhone.
· In 2024, Apple Intelligence and ChatGPT were integrated into iOS 18.
examples_en: Siri was the world's first widely commercialized AI voice assistant.
The iPhone's Neural Engine can process trillions of AI operations per second.
Core ML allows developers to seamlessly deploy models to the iPhone.

terms.definition_short: Arthur Samuel 让「机器从经验中变好」变成可运行的程序，机器学习从这里有了直观样本。
terms.definition_short_en: Arthur Samuel turned the concept of machines improving from experience into a working program, providing an intuitive early example of machine learning.

terms.definition_short: Arturo Rosenblueth 把生物行为、目标和反馈带入控制论前史。
terms.definition_short_en: Arturo Rosenblueth was a physiologist who introduced biological behavior, purpose, and feedback into the prehistory of cybernetics.

terms.definition_short: Atlassian：Jira Confluence Trello Loom 的母公司——澳洲 SaaS 双子星。
terms.definition_short_en: Atlassian is an Australian SaaS giant and the parent company behind widely used workplace collaboration tools like Jira, Confluence, Trello, and Loom.

terms.definition_short: 波士顿动力代表着机器人从工厂走向野外——动态平衡能力让它成为机器人运动的标杆。
terms.definition_short_en: Boston Dynamics represents the transition of robots from factory floors to unstructured environments, with its dynamic balance capabilities setting the benchmark for robotic mobility.
terms.back_en: An American robotics company renowned for dynamic balance and mobility. From the BigDog military quadruped to the Atlas humanoid and the commercial Spot robot dog, its products consistently push robotic movement to new heights.
terms.definition_long_en:
Boston Dynamics was founded in 1992 by Marc Raibert as a spin-off from the MIT Leg Laboratory. The company's core philosophy is that robots must first learn to move before they learn to think.

Its product line includes BigDog, a military quadruped capable of carrying heavy loads across rugged terrain; Atlas, a humanoid robot that can perform parkour, backflips, and dance routines; Spot, a commercial robot dog used for construction site inspections, hospital disinfection during the pandemic, and offshore platform monitoring; and Stretch, a logistics robot designed specifically for moving boxes in warehouses.

The company's ownership has changed several times: acquired by Google in 2013, taken over by SoftBank in 2017, and majority-owned by Hyundai Motor Group in 2020 (for $1.1 billion). Each transition brought strategic shifts—from military applications to commercial use, and from research demonstrations to productization.

Boston Dynamics' technical moat lies in dynamic balance. Maintaining stability on uneven terrain requires a millisecond-level perception-control-execution loop, a capability that remains difficult for other robotics companies to replicate.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Boston Dynamics represents the transition of robots from controlled factory settings to unpredictable real-world environments. Its dynamic balance capabilities have made it the industry benchmark for robotic mobility, fundamentally redefining the public imagination of what robots are capable of doing.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the company that makes robots do parkour and backflips, founded by Marc Raibert in 1992.
terms.example_en:
· The Atlas humanoid robot can perform parkour and backflips.
· The Spot robot dog is used for construction site inspections and hospital disinfection.
· The BigDog quadruped was designed for the military to navigate rugged terrain.
· Ownership changes: Google (2013) → SoftBank (2017) → Hyundai (2020).
examples_en: The Atlas humanoid robot can perform parkour and backflips.
The Spot robot dog is used for construction site inspections and hospital disinfection.
The BigDog quadruped was designed for the military to navigate rugged terrain.

terms.definition_short: 布朗运动：1827 年布朗发现的粒子在水中的无规则运动——看似随机却成为 AI 扩散模型的基础数学。
terms.definition_short_en: Brownian motion refers to the random movement of particles in water discovered in 1827, a seemingly random phenomenon that later became the foundational mathematics for AI diffusion models.

terms.definition_short: Canva：澳洲 SaaS 双子星之二——让任何人都能设计的在线设计平台。
terms.definition_short_en: An online design platform—often considered one of Australia's twin SaaS stars—that empowers anyone to create designs without professional training.

terms.definition_short: 普林斯顿计算语言学家，全球 WordNet 协会主席。她向李飞飞介绍了 WordNet，间接催生了 ImageNet。
terms.definition_short_en: A computational linguist at Princeton and president of the Global WordNet Association, who introduced Fei-Fei Li to WordNet and indirectly catalyzed the creation of ImageNet.

terms.definition_short: 加州理工学院计算神经科学家，李飞飞的第二位博导。穿荧光衬衫、把头发染成绿色的自由派科学家。
terms.definition_short_en: A computational neuroscientist at Caltech and Fei-Fei Li's second PhD advisor, known as a free-spirited scientist who wore neon shirts and dyed his hair green.

terms.definition_short: Claude Shannon 奠定信息论，把信息、编码、噪声和通信变成可计算的问题。
terms.definition_short_en: Claude Shannon founded information theory, transforming abstract concepts like information, coding, noise, and communication into rigorous, computable mathematical problems.

terms.definition_short: Dario Amodei 是 Anthropic 和 Claude 路线的根本组织者，把模型产品、安全叙事和政策立场绑在一起。
terms.definition_short_en: Dario Amodei is the principal architect behind Anthropic and the Claude models, uniquely intertwining product development, AI safety narratives, and policy advocacy.
terms.back_en: Co-founder and CEO of Anthropic. Formerly VP of Research at OpenAI, he left in 2021 over concerns that OpenAI's commercialization path lacked sufficient investment in safety, subsequently building Anthropic into the leading "safety-first frontier model company."
terms.definition_long_en:
Dario's story must be viewed through the lens of the fierce competition among foundation model companies.
Serving as VP of Research at OpenAI from 2016 to 2021, he led safety research for GPT-2 and GPT-3. In 2021, he and his sister Daniela left to found Anthropic. Their publicly stated reason for the departure was dissatisfaction with OpenAI's shift from a non-profit to a "capped-profit" structure, feeling that the push for commercialization came at the expense of adequate investment in AI safety.
Anthropic's strategy is distinct: it develops frontier models like Claude and enterprise products while heavily emphasizing alignment, interpretability, evaluation, and safety tiers. Constitutional AI, the Responsible Scaling Policy, and systematic red-teaming form the core of Anthropic's safety research.
This dual focus positions Dario as both a tech CEO and a leading voice in AI safety narratives. He frequently discusses frontier model capabilities alongside risk governance, US technological leadership, and chip export controls. In 2025, he published the essay "On DeepSeek and Export Controls," explicitly tying AI competition to geopolitics. This stance naturally courts controversy, as it intertwines technical roadmaps, commercial rivalry, regulatory lobbying, and geopolitical strategy.
Understanding Dario means understanding Anthropic's complex role: simultaneously building Claude products while vying for authority as the definitive "safety-first frontier model company."
terms.why_it_matters_en: He clarifies the strategic direction behind Claude: pushing for strong model capabilities and reliable enterprise products while securing a foothold in safety narratives and policy influence. Understanding Amodei explains why Anthropic consistently places product development and AI safety on the same table.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember him as the safety-focused architect behind Claude—the former OpenAI VP who walked away in 2021.
terms.example_en:
· 2016-2021: Served as VP of Research at OpenAI, leading safety research for GPT-2 and GPT-3.
· 2021: Left OpenAI with Daniela Amodei to found Anthropic.
· Constitutional AI, safety tiers, and model evaluations form the core of Anthropic's public narrative.
· 2025: Published "On DeepSeek and Export Controls," explicitly linking AI competition with geopolitics.
examples_en: Anthropic competes in the frontier model race with Claude.
Constitutional AI, safety tiers, and model evaluations form the core of Anthropic's public narrative.

terms.definition_short: DeepMind：Google 的 AI 研究实验室，做出了 AlphaGo、AlphaFold、Gemini——拿过两次诺贝尔奖。
terms.definition_short_en: Google's AI research laboratory that created AlphaGo, AlphaFold, and Gemini, and whose groundbreaking work has produced two Nobel laureates.

terms.definition_short: DeepSeek：中国 AI 公司深度求索，2024-2025 年用开源模型连续冲击全球 AI 格局。
terms.definition_short_en: A Chinese AI company that disrupted the global AI landscape in 2024 and 2025 by releasing highly capable and cost-effective open-source foundation models.

terms.definition_short: DeepSeek-V3：DeepSeek 2024 年的旗舰模型——671B MoE 参数——每次推理只激活 37B。
terms.definition_short_en: DeepSeek's flagship 2024 model featuring a 671-billion-parameter Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture that activates only 37 billion parameters during inference.

terms.definition_short: Demis Hassabis 是把游戏智能、认知科学和科学发现接成一条 AGI 路线的人，也是 DeepMind 的根本组织者。
terms.definition_short_en: Demis Hassabis is the primary architect of DeepMind, bridging game AI, cognitive science, and scientific discovery into a cohesive roadmap toward artificial general intelligence.
terms.front_en: Who is Demis Hassabis in the AI world?
terms.back_en: The co-founder of DeepMind. A chess prodigy turned game designer and cognitive neuroscientist, he led AI's evolution from mastering board games to solving real-world scientific challenges, winning the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold.
terms.definition_long_en:
Hassabis's strength lies in a rare combination of expertise: he understands games, the human brain, and how to organize research into a long-term corporate roadmap.

A chess prodigy, he reached master standard at age 13, becoming the second-youngest chess master in the world at the time. He later transitioned to game development, working at Bullfrog Productions and founding Elixir Studios, with notable titles like *Theme Park* and *Republic: The Revolution*. These experiences taught him how complex systems with clear rules evolve. He then earned a PhD in cognitive neuroscience at University College London (UCL), studying the neural basis of memory and imagination. This interdisciplinary background made him uniquely equipped to understand both intelligence and engineering.

DeepMind grew from this foundation. AlphaGo first proved that AI could use search, reinforcement learning, and self-play to discover strategies unseen by human Go masters. AlphaFold later extended this capability to the life sciences, revolutionizing protein structure prediction and earning Hassabis and John Jumper the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
terms.why_it_matters_en: He guided AI's evolution from mastering board games to solving real-world scientific challenges. His trajectory demonstrates that the true value of AI extends far beyond chatbots and generative content, reaching into the discovery of hidden laws within complex systems.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember him as the man who trained intelligence in games, brought it into science, and won a Nobel Prize.
terms.example_en:
· Reached chess master standard at age 13, becoming the second-youngest in the world at the time.
· Developed games like *Theme Park*, mastering complex systems with clear rules.
· Earned a PhD in cognitive neuroscience from UCL, researching memory and imagination.
· Led the creation of AlphaGo, which discovered Go strategies unseen by human masters.
· Spearheaded AlphaFold, applying learning systems to protein structure prediction and transforming life sciences.
· Awarded the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside John Jumper.
examples_en: AlphaGo enabled AI to discover Go strategies previously unseen by human masters.
AlphaFold applied learning systems to protein structure prediction, directly transforming research in the life sciences.

terms.definition_short: Donald Hebb 把学习和神经连接变化联系起来，留下了「共同激活，连接增强」的直觉。
terms.definition_short_en: Donald Hebb linked learning to changes in neural connections, leaving behind the enduring intuition that "neurons that fire together, wire together."

terms.definition_short: Edward Feigenbaum 推动专家系统路线，把领域专家的知识整理成机器可用的规则。
terms.definition_short_en: Edward Feigenbaum pioneered the expert system approach, organizing the specialized knowledge of domain experts into machine-usable rules.

terms.definition_short: Frank Rosenblatt 让神经网络第一次站上聚光灯，感知机证明机器可以从样本中学习分类。
terms.definition_short_en: Frank Rosenblatt brought neural networks into the spotlight for the first time, using the perceptron to prove that machines could learn to classify data from examples.

terms.definition_short: Garry Kasparov 是 1985-2000 年世界国际象棋冠军，1997 年与 IBM Deep Blue 的对决是 AI 史标志性事件。
terms.definition_short_en: Garry Kasparov was the World Chess Champion from 1985 to 2000, and his 1997 match against IBM's Deep Blue remains a landmark event in AI history.

terms.definition_short: Geoffrey Hinton 是深度学习复兴的根本人物：他守住神经网络长线，见证 AlexNet 爆发，后来又成为 AI 风险警告中最有分量的声音。
terms.definition_short_en: Geoffrey Hinton is a foundational figure in the deep learning revival. He championed neural networks through their long winter, oversaw the AlexNet breakthrough, and later became one of the most prominent voices warning about AI risks.
terms.front_en: Who is Geoffrey Hinton in the field of AI?
terms.back_en: He championed neural networks from their lowest point to their breakthrough. Backpropagation, AlexNet, and mentoring Ilya Sutskever all trace back to him. A 2018 Turing Award and 2024 Nobel Prize laureate, he later became a leading voice warning of AI risks.
terms.definition_long_en:
Hinton's significance lies not just in his "AI Godfather" moniker, but in his dedication to a once-unpopular approach until it triggered the modern AI boom. He long believed multi-layer neural networks could learn representations directly from data. In 1986, the backpropagation paper by Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams brought multi-layer network training back into focus.

By 2012, Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever from Hinton's lab created AlexNet, achieving groundbreaking results on ImageNet. This milestone connected data, GPUs, backpropagation, and neural networks into the primary trajectory of modern AI. The mentorship dynamic is crucial: Sutskever was Hinton's student at the University of Toronto. The history of AlexNet, GPU training, and the deep learning revival inevitably circles back to Hinton, representing a continuous thread of mentorship, conviction, and engineering breakthroughs. He held onto the belief that neural networks would awaken at scale until the evidence finally emerged.

In 2018, he received the ACM A.M. Turing Award alongside Yoshua Bengio and Yann LeCun. In 2024, he and John Hopfield were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for foundational discoveries enabling machine learning with artificial neural networks.

In 2023, Hinton left Google to publicly warn about AI risks, expressing concern that digital intelligence might grow stronger in ways fundamentally different from the human brain, and urging the world to take AI safety seriously.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Understanding Hinton connects several crucial threads: why neural networks were once unpopular, why AlexNet was a breakthrough, the importance of his mentorship of Ilya Sutskever, why a Nobel Prize was awarded for foundational machine learning work, and why the earliest pioneer of deep learning later issued serious warnings about AI risks.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember him as the firekeeper who sounded the alarm: he guarded the spark of neural networks until they ignited, then warned the fire might burn out of control.

· Ilya Sutskever was one of Hinton's students in Toronto; the AlexNet breakthrough was the result of this mentorship converging with ImageNet data and GPU engineering capabilities.

· In 2024, Hinton was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for foundational discoveries in machine learning with artificial neural networks.

terms.definition_short_en: Google Brain was a driving force behind the deep learning renaissance, producing industry-altering innovations ranging from unsupervised cat recognition to the Transformer architecture.

terms.definition_short_en: "GPT Meta" refers to Meta's series of open-weight foundation models, including LLaMA, LLaMA 2, LLaMA 3, and the 2025 release of LLaMA 4.

terms.definition_short: 赫伯特·西蒙（1916-2001）是 20 世纪罕见的跨学科通才——唯一同时获得图灵奖和诺贝尔经济学奖的人。他是 AI 奠基人、认知科学创始人、行为经济学开创者。
terms.definition_short_en: Herbert Simon (1916–2001) was a rare 20th-century interdisciplinary polymath and the only person to win both the Turing Award and the Nobel Prize in Economics. He was a founding father of AI, cognitive science, and behavioral economics.

terms.definition_short: 哈佛神经科学家。1959 年通过猫脑实验发现视觉皮层分层次处理信息，1981 年获得诺贝尔奖。他们是 CNN 的生物学蓝图来源。
terms.definition_short_en: Harvard neuroscientists who discovered hierarchical information processing in the visual cortex through cat brain experiments in 1959. Awarded the 1981 Nobel Prize, their work provided the biological blueprint for CNNs.

terms.definition_short: Hugging Face：AI 界的 GitHub——模型、数据集、demo 全在上面，开源社区的中心。
terms.definition_short_en: The GitHub of AI—a central hub for the open-source community where models, datasets, and demos are hosted and shared.
terms.back_en: The GitHub of AI. Started in France in 2016, its platform grew faster than its original product after open-sourcing a BERT implementation in 2018. By 2024, it hosted over 500,000 models and 100,000 datasets, reaching a $4.5 billion valuation.
terms.definition_long_en:
What is Hugging Face? It is the GitHub of the AI world.
Founded in France in 2016, Hugging Face initially started as a chatbot app. In 2018, they open-sourced a PyTorch implementation of BERT and built a model-sharing platform alongside it. The platform ended up growing faster than the product itself—by 2024, it hosted over 500,000 models and 100,000 datasets.
The Hugging Face ecosystem relies on a core trio: Models (for downloading pre-trained weights), Datasets (for downloading and preprocessing training data), and Spaces (for deploying demos that can be tested directly in a browser). Whenever a new AI paper is published, someone usually uploads the weights and a demo to Hugging Face within a week.
The Transformers library is the true engine behind Hugging Face, allowing developers to load any model, tokenize text, and run inference with just a few lines of Python code, seamlessly supporting both PyTorch and TensorFlow. Valued at $4.5 billion in 2024, Hugging Face has attracted investments from Google, Amazon, and NVIDIA, all driven by the same rationale: it is the primary control point of the open-source AI ecosystem.
terms.why_it_matters_en: Hugging Face is the epicenter of the open-source AI community. Whether you need to find model weights, source datasets, or test out new models, it all starts here.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember it as the GitHub for AI models—where the world shares its models.

· The Transformers library: load any model, tokenize, and run inference with a few lines of code, supporting both PyTorch and TensorFlow.
· Valued at $4.5 billion in 2024 with backing from Google, Amazon, and NVIDIA—acting as the control point of the open-source ecosystem.
· The core trio: go to Models for weights, use the Trainer API for fine-tuning, and visit Spaces to test models.

terms.definition_short: Ian Goodfellow 提出 GAN，把生成式 AI 早期的「造假与鉴定」训练游戏推到台前。
terms.definition_short_en: Ian Goodfellow introduced GANs, bringing the "forgery and detection" training dynamic to the forefront of early generative AI.

terms.definition_short: Ilya Sutskever 是 OpenAI 联合创始人、前首席科学家，AlexNet 发明者，GPT 系列和 ChatGPT 的根本推动者。
terms.definition_short_en: Ilya Sutskever is a co-founder and former Chief Scientist of OpenAI, co-creator of AlexNet, and a fundamental driving force behind the GPT series and ChatGPT.

terms.definition_short: James Lighthill 的报告让英国 AI 研究降温，是第一次 AI 寒冬的重要外部评审节点。
terms.definition_short_en: James Lighthill's 1973 report cooled AI research in the UK, serving as a crucial external review milestone that triggered the first AI winter.

terms.definition_short: Jensen Huang 是把 GPU、CUDA 和数据中心推成 AI 基础设施的人，NVIDIA 城墙的根本组织者。
terms.definition_short_en: Jensen Huang is the architect behind NVIDIA's competitive moat, transforming GPUs, the CUDA platform, and data centers into the foundational infrastructure of modern AI.
terms.front_en: Why is Jensen Huang central to any discussion on AI compute?
terms.back_en: Jensen Huang transformed NVIDIA from a graphics chipmaker into an AI infrastructure powerhouse. GPUs, CUDA, data centers, and AI Factories all stem from his core realization: if deep learning continues to scale, AI will relentlessly demand more compute.
terms.definition_long_en:
Jensen Huang's impact stems from his long-term industrial foresight at NVIDIA. Born in Tainan in 1963, he immigrated to the US at age 9. In 1993, he co-founded NVIDIA with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, initially focusing on gaming graphics cards.

He grasped a fundamental truth: if deep learning continued to scale deeper and larger, AI would relentlessly require more data, larger models, and stronger compute. Following the breakthrough of AlexNet, he recognized that GPUs, CUDA, interconnects, software libraries, and data centers could become the foundation of AI.

CUDA serves as the critical moat in this strategy. Because developers, research labs, cloud providers, and enterprises built their code, workflows, and libraries on the NVIDIA ecosystem, the GPU became the bedrock of AI computing. Competitors like AMD, Google TPU, and AWS Trainium have attempted to bypass CUDA, but over a decade of accumulated toolchains and optimizations remains difficult to replicate.

Understanding Jensen Huang means understanding the industrial reality behind the AI wave: no matter how smart a model is, it must run on physical machines, real electricity, massive data centers, and robust software ecosystems. In 2024, NVIDIA's market capitalization briefly surpassed $3 trillion, joining Apple and Microsoft as one of the world's three most valuable companies.
terms.why_it_matters_en: He transformed AI compute from a hardware business into an infrastructure business. Today's large language model competition, AI Factories, data center arms races, and the CUDA moat can all be traced back to his strategic foresight.
terms.memory_hook_en: Remember him as the man who turned the GPU into the engine of AI—founding NVIDIA in 1993 and building the CUDA moat.
terms.example_en:
· After AlexNet, NVIDIA identified deep learning as a long-term opportunity.
· CUDA makes it difficult for developers to leave the NVIDIA ecosystem—AMD and Google TPU attempt to bypass it but find it hard to replicate.
· The "AI Factory" concept frames data centers as factories continuously generating tokens.
· In 2024, NVIDIA's market cap briefly exceeded $3 trillion, ranking alongside Apple and Microsoft.
examples_en: After AlexNet, NVIDIA identified deep learning as a long-term opportunity.
CUDA makes it difficult for developers to leave the NVIDIA ecosystem.
The "AI Factory" concept frames data centers as factories continuously generating tokens.

terms.definition_short: JS 散度：KL 散度的对称版本——比较两个概率分布有多像。GAN 的损失函数最初就是最小化 JS 散度。比 KL 好在对两个方向一致——但训练仍难。
terms.definition_short_en: JS divergence is a symmetric version of KL divergence used to measure the similarity between two probability distributions. The original GAN loss function minimized JS divergence. It improves upon KL by being symmetric, though training remains difficult.

terms.definition_short: 李飞飞的第一位博士生，ImageNet 数据工程和技术实现的主力。他算出手动标注需要 19 年，推动了众包方案。
terms.definition_short_en: Fei-Fei Li's first PhD student and the primary force behind ImageNet's data engineering and technical implementation. He calculated that manual labeling would take 19 years and championed the crowdsourcing solution.

terms.definition_short: 伯克利计算机视觉泰斗，佩罗纳的前导师。他告诉辛顿去「试试 ImageNet」，间接促成了 AlexNet 的诞生。
terms.definition_short_en: A UC Berkeley computer vision pioneer and Pietro Perona's former advisor. He told Geoffrey Hinton to "try ImageNet," indirectly leading to the creation of AlexNet.

terms.definition_short: John McCarthy 给 AI 起名、搭会议、造 Lisp，让人工智能从想法变成一个研究共同体。
terms.definition_short_en: John McCarthy coined the term "Artificial Intelligence," organized its foundational conference, and invented Lisp, transforming AI from scattered ideas into a cohesive research community.

terms.definition_short: John von Neumann 给现代计算机搭出底层骨架，让后来的 AI 程序有了可运行的机器基础。
terms.definition_short_en: John von Neumann designed the foundational architecture of modern computers, providing the essential hardware basis upon which all subsequent AI programs run.

terms.definition_short: Joseph Weizenbaum 写出 ELIZA，也成为 AI 过度拟人化的早期批评者。
terms.definition_short_en: Joseph Weizenbaum created the early chatbot ELIZA and later became a prominent critic of AI anthropomorphism.

terms.definition_short: 普林斯顿 CS 教授，微处理器架构先驱。他是 ImageNet 的第一个坚定支持者，在所有人反对时捐了一套工作站。
terms.definition_short_en: A Princeton computer science professor and pioneer in microprocessor architecture. He was the first staunch supporter of ImageNet, donating a workstation to the project when everyone else opposed it.

terms.definition_short: 柯洁是中国围棋世界冠军，2017 年 5 月以 0:3 负于 AlphaGo，是围棋作为「人类智慧最后高地」被 AI 攻破的标志性事件之二。
terms.definition_short_en: Ke Jie is a Chinese Go world champion whose 0:3 defeat by AlphaGo in May 2017 served as the second landmark event of AI conquering Go, the "last bastion of human intelligence."

terms.definition_short: 贝尔实验室是计算机科学史上的「黄埔军校」——孕育的信息基础设施比任何一个机构都多。
terms.definition_short_en: Bell Labs is the cradle of modern computer science, having incubated more foundational information infrastructure than any other institution in history.

terms.definition_short: 卡内基梅隆大学是 AI 历史中「动手派」的代表，与 MIT、斯坦福的理论路线形成鲜明对比。
terms.definition_short_en: Carnegie Mellon University represents the "hands-on" faction in AI history, standing in stark contrast to the theoretical approaches of MIT and Stanford.

terms.definition_short: DARPA（美国国防部高级研究计划局）——美国国防部的研发机构，AI 和互联网都受其资助。
terms.definition_short_en: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is the R&D arm of the U.S. Department of Defense, responsible for funding foundational technologies including artificial intelligence and the internet.

terms.definition_short: Google 是同时做 AI（取代人类决策）和 IA（增强人类能力）两派的科技巨头。
terms.definition_short_en: Google is a tech giant that simultaneously pursues both AI (replacing human decision-making) and IA (augmenting human capabilities).

terms.definition_short: MIT AI 实验室是 60 年代美国 AI 研究的双中心之一，与斯坦福 SAIL 形成对立。
terms.definition_short_en: The MIT AI Lab was one of the two major hubs for American AI research in the 1960s, serving as the East Coast counterpart to Stanford's SAIL.

terms.definition_short: 斯坦福研究所 SRI——Shakey 机器人和恩格尔巴特 NLS 系统的诞生地。
terms.definition_short_en: The Stanford Research Institute (SRI) is the birthplace of the Shakey robot and Douglas Engelbart's pioneering NLS system.

terms.term: 斯坦福 AI 实验室 SAIL
terms.term_zh: 斯坦福 AI 实验室 SAIL
terms.definition_short: 斯坦福 AI 实验室（SAIL）——麦卡锡创立的西海岸 AI 旗杆。
terms.definition_short_en: The Stanford AI Lab (SAIL), founded by John McCarthy, serves as the West Coast flagship of artificial intelligence research.
